crossfield_g4_findings: The general process borrowed here is "a naive/conventional pool converts into a long-lived antigen-experienced memory pool by clonal expansion and differentiation." All three home fields have already had their reckoning with this arrow, and all three verdicts land against P1. T CELL — (a) The gold-standard method exists and gives the OPPOSITE answer in NK cells. Buchholz VR et al. Science 2013;340:630, PMID 23493420 (with Gerlach C et al. Science 2013;340:635, PMID 23493421) did in vivo single-cell fate mapping of naive CD8 T cells and found "striking variability of immune responses derived from individual CD8+ T cells", with single naive cells generating BOTH short-lived effector and long-lived memory progeny along a linear developmental path, and robust immunity requiring "the initial recruitment of multiple precursors." The same group (Buchholz is senior author on both Grassmann 2019 and Flommersfeld 2021) then applied that exact method to NK cells and found the opposite — fate-RESTRICTED, non-diversifying clones tracing to two pre-existing lineages. So the NK field imported the T-cell "naive -> effector -> memory linear differentiation" narrative, and when the T-cell field's own definitive assay was finally run on NK cells it did not reproduce. (b) The memory repertoire is SELECTED from a pre-existing affinity spectrum, not converted. Zehn D, Lee SY, Bevan MJ. Nature 2009;458:211, PMID 19182777: clones across a broad avidity range are all recruited, and the pool "subsequently matures in affinity owing to the more prolonged expansion of high-affinity T-cell clones." This is precisely the mechanism Adams 2019 (Ly49H avidity), Grassmann 2019 (Ly49H surface density) and Ruckert 2022 (NKG2C density) each rediscovered for NK cells — i.e. the null hypothesis P1 must exclude is a 2009 T-cell result, and P1's evidence base never excludes it. (c) VIRTUAL / ANTIGEN-INEXPERIENCED MEMORY-PHENOTYPE T CELLS are the exact structural trap. Reviewed in Virtual Memory CD8+ T Cells: Origin and Beyond, PMC9835308 (2022); primary mechanism in Sosinowski T et al. J Immunol 2013, PMID 23355737, "CD8alpha+ dendritic cell trans presentation of IL-15 to naive CD8+ T cells produces antigen-inexperienced T cells in the periphery with memory phenotype." A cell carrying the full antigen-experienced surface signature that never met the antigen. This is the direct analogue of Ruckert 2022's "naive NKG2C+" NK cells, present at comparable frequency in HCMV-seronegative and HCMV-positive donors and spanning CD56bright and CD56dim. The T-cell field's settled lesson: a memory-phenotype marker set is not evidence of an antigen-driven conversion event. ILC — Vonarbourg C, ... Diefenbach A. Immunity 2010;33:736, PMID 21093318 is the experiment the NK field has never run for NKG2C, published a full year BEFORE Lopez-Verges 2011. Using adoptive transfer of genetically tagged LTi-like cells plus Rorc genetic lineage tracing, they showed "NKR-RORgammat+ innate lymphocytes but not NK cells were direct progenitors to NKR+RORgammat+ cells in vivo" — a fate map that both identifies the true precursor AND explicitly excludes the presumed one. The broader ILC lesson is the same error mode as Guma 2006's HCMV-infected fibroblast cocultures: cytokine-driven "plasticity" between marker-defined ILC states in vitro repeatedly failed to predict in vivo ontogeny until fate mapping and parabiosis adjudicated. MYELOID — this is the fatal collision. (a) Monocyte -> tissue macrophage is the canonical overturned "A becomes B", held as dogma for roughly forty years on exactly the evidence classes carrying P1: marker overlap, kinetics, and bulk transfer. Hashimoto D et al. Immunity 2013;38:792, PMID 23601688 states it outright — "Despite accumulating evidence suggesting local self-maintenance of tissue macrophages in the steady state, the dogma remains that tissue macrophages derive from monocytes. Using parabiosis and fate-mapping approaches, we confirmed that monocytes do not show significant contribution to tissue macrophages" — and Yona S et al. Immunity 2013;38:79, PMID 23273845 (CX3CR1-CreER fate mapping) showed the resident populations "are established prior to birth and maintain themselves subsequently during adulthood independent of replenishment by blood monocytes." A PRE-EXISTING, SELF-MAINTAINING POPULATION was mistaken for a conversion product for four decades. Critically, the same Yona paper validated a REAL conversion in the same system (Ly6C+ -> Ly6C- monocytes), proving the method discriminates true arrows from false ones — so its absence in the NK field is a gap, not an impossibility. (b) Innate immune memory is written at the PROGENITOR level, not by converting a mature cell. Kaufmann E et al. Cell 2018;172:176, PMID 29328912: BCG reprograms HSCs and MPPs, and "BCG-educated HSCs generate epigenetically modified macrophages", with parabiosis, chimeric mice and adoptive transfer showing the training is sustained through the stem-cell compartment. Map that onto P1 and it is directly fatal: Ruckert 2022's own negative control says mtDNA clonal marks in the conventional NK compartment "do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level", and HCMV establishes latency in CD34+ HSPCs. A progenitor-level HCMV imprint reproduces EVERY observation in P1's evidence base — elevated NKG2C+ frequency, clonal marks, adaptive epigenetic remodelling, transplant-associated expansions — without any mature conventional NK cell ever converting. No study in P1's evidence base excludes it, and the human HSCT/UCBT data the row correctly declined to promote to OBS_TRANSFER are exactly the data that would be confounded by it. This progenitor-level alternative is invisible to NK keywords and is the single largest unexamined hole in the row.

strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION OF A PRE-EXISTING HYPER-RESPONSIVE SUBSET RATHER THAN CONVERSION. Every experiment in this literature tracks a BULK population with a non-clonal label — a dilutable dye (CFSE, Cooper 2009), a congenic allele shared by millions of cells (CD45.1/CD45.2, Keppel 2013 / Ni 2012), or an HLA mismatch shared by the whole graft (Romee 2016). None of these can distinguish "each NK cell converted" from "the responsive minority survived, homed and expanded". Three independent lines make selection concrete: (1) IL-12/15/18 preactivation itself kills NK cells — Terren et al. 2023 Front Immunol (PMID 37575238) report that "upon IL-12/15/18 stimulation the viability of NK cells decreased", with raised mitochondrial superoxide and impaired mitophagy, so the preactivation step is itself a survival filter; (2) Romee 2012's own data map the memory-like IFN-gamma response onto markers that exist BEFORE preactivation — CD94, NKG2A, NKG2C and CD69 high with CD57 and KIR absent, i.e. the less-differentiated pre-existing compartment; Foltz et al. 2024 Sci Immunol (PMID 38941480) reach the same place by Waddington-OT/CellRank fate-probability inference (eML-1 from CD56bright, eML-2 from CD56dim) with NO barcoding and no lineage tracing; (3) in patients, Shapiro et al. 2022 JCI (PMID 35349491) found that "Patients 3 and 4 both exhibited a dominance of NK clusters on day +28 and day +60 that constituted a minor portion of the infusion product" — disproportionate outgrowth of a minor pre-existing subset, which is the selection model, and they state outright that "there was no traceable marker in the infused CIML NK cells, it was not possible to use donor chimerism or other direct means to track the infused NK cells." SECOND ALTERNATIVE — the recovered state is not "memory" but a persistently activated / homeostatically expanded effector state: Ni et al. 2012 JEM (PMID 23209317) used the same IL-12/15/18 cocktail with proper CD45.1 congenic tracking and found cells that persist >=3 months but are KLRG1-hi, granzyme B-hi and phenotypically mature, whose proliferation is IL-2- and CD4-T-cell-dependent and which require 5 Gy host irradiation to work — the opposite of Cooper's granzyme-B-negative, non-cytotoxic resting "memory" cell. Keppel 2013 saw KLRG1 rise on BOTH preactivated and control cells after homeostatic expansion and conceded in print that "these enhanced responses could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response." THIRD ALTERNATIVE (human trial only) — lymphodepletion plus cytokine support, not preactivation, drives the in vivo expansion and the remissions.

crossfield_g4_findings: MYELOID (trained immunity — the field CIML NK explicitly borrows from; the 2022 Front Immunol CIML review PMID 35603208 says outright that CIML NK "resemble the trained immunity observed in myeloid cells"). The myeloid field ran this exact experiment first and discovered its own fatal artefact: the long-lived "trained" peripheral cell is NOT the cell that was trained. Cirovic B et al., Cell Host Microbe 2020;28:322-334, PMID 32544459 / PMC7295478 (20 healthy volunteers, 15 BCG / 5 placebo, bone-marrow aspirates + blood at d0/d14/d90) states verbatim that HSPC reprogramming "allows for a persistent induction of a trained immunity phenotype of CD14+ monocytes, BEYOND THE INDIVIDUAL CELL'S LIFESPAN," with "BCG vaccination imprint[ing] a persistent transcriptomic myeloid bias on human HSPCs." Same conclusion from Kaufmann E et al., Cell 2018;172:176-190, PMID 29328912 ("BCG Educates Hematopoietic Stem Cells"); Khan N et al., Cell 2020;183:752-770, PMID 33125891; Kalafati L et al., Cell 2020;183:771-785, PMID 33125892. COLLISION: mouse CIML is actually protected here — Keppel 2013's Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts cannot generate new NK cells, so donor persistence out to 4 months is real. But the HUMAN CIML persistence claims are made in exactly the configuration the myeloid field showed to be uninterpretable: a marrow actively producing new donor NK cells, under IL-15 superagonist support, with NO tracking marker (Berrien-Elliott 2022 STM PMID 35196021: "HLA-based NK cell tracking was not possible"; Bednarski 2022 Blood PMID 34871371, viSNE phenotype only; Shapiro 2022 JCI PMID 35349491, "no traceable marker"). The myeloid field's answer to "is the persisting trained cell the same cell?" was NO — and human CIML has never run the equivalent control. T CELL. Three collisions. (a) The pre-existing memory-phenotype compartment. Haluszczak C et al., J Exp Med 2009;206:435-448, PMID 19188498 / PMC2646575 showed antigen-specific memory-phenotype CD8 T cells exist in UNIMMUNIZED mice "bearing markers of homeostatic expansion"; White JT et al., Nat Commun 2016;7:11291, PMID 27097762 / PMC4844673 showed these virtual-memory cells are "15-25% of the unprimed CD8 pool", arise "in an IL-15-dependent manner", are found in human cord blood so "it was not necessary for them to be derived from antigen-experienced memory T cells", and "are capable of mediating potent immunological protection... even in the absence of their cognate antigen". The T cell field's mandatory null hypothesis for any "we induced memory" claim is therefore a pre-existing, IL-15-driven, functionally-memory compartment that was never converted. CIML NK has run no equivalent control — and Romee 2012's own marker data place the ML recall response on CD94/NKG2A/NKG2C-hi, CD57/KIR-negative less-differentiated cells, i.e. the pre-existing IL-15-responsive compartment. (b) Bulk transfer cannot license per-cell statements. Buchholz VR et al., Science 2013;340:630-635, PMID 23493420, "Disparate individual fates compose robust CD8+ T cell immunity" — single-cell fate mapping showed individual naive T cells give wildly divergent progeny, so the average behaviour of a bulk transferred population says nothing about what any cell did. Cooper 2009 (CFSE bulk), Keppel 2013 and Ni 2012 (congenic bulk) are all bulk transfers. (c) The mechanism collision. Cooper's own ref 21, Bird JJ et al., Immunity 1998;9:229-237, established that Th1 IFN-gamma competence is acquired THROUGH cell division via epigenetic remodelling. Cooper 2009 Fig 4 finds the opposite in NK — generation 0 (never divided) equals generations 1-3 — and the authors state the contrast explicitly ("This aspect is in contrast to CD4+ T cells"). Read against the T cell field, a division-independent, dose/duration-graded (5 h weaker than overnight), decay-prone effect is the signature of persistent PRIMING (a long-lived signalling/protein state), not of differentiation; Cooper concedes the alternative in print ("Alternatively, an increased activation time may allow for a higher percentage of NK cells to differentiate into memory-like cells"), and Keppel 2013 concedes "these enhanced responses could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response." ILC. (a) The ILC memory literature has the survival-selection artefact written into its own model: Martinez-Gonzalez I et al., Immunity 2016;45:198-208, PMID 27421705 — ILC2s "proliferated and secreted cytokines upon initial stimulation with allergen or IL-33, and this phase was followed by a CONTRACTION PHASE... Some ILC2s persisted long after the resolution of the inflammation as allergen-experienced ILC2s and responded to unrelated allergens more potently than naive ILC2s." The memory-like cells are by construction the SURVIVORS of a die-off — the same structure Terren 2023 (PMID 37575238) documents for IL-12/15/18-treated NK, i.e. the preactivation step is a survival filter. Same experimental design as CIML (bulk transfer + heterologous recall assay), same unexcluded alternative. (b) The ILC field's methodological standard is stricter than the NK field's: apparent ILC3->ILC1 conversion (e.g. Mucosal Immunol 2021, PMID 33214656; c-Maf, J Exp Med 2020, PMID 31570496) is adjudicated with genetic fate-mapping reporters, not marker overlap or transfer. (c) The single most relevant ILC result sits on the NK/ILC1 boundary: Flommersfeld 2021 Immunity, PMID 34437840, single-NK-cell fate mapping split what the field assumed was one adaptive-like NK differentiation pathway into a cNK lineage and an ILC1-like lineage. NET BEARING ON P2: all three fields independently converged on the same rule — a "memory-like" state defined by a bulk recall assay plus a persistence timecourse is NOT adjudicable without either (i) single-cell/clonal fate mapping, or (ii) a host that provably cannot generate the cell de novo. Mouse CIML satisfies (ii) only (Keppel 2013). Human CIML satisfies neither.

claim_text: Liver memory NK: existence and origin
species: Mouse for all memory/origin experiments: C57BL/6, BALB/c, Rag1-/-, Rag2-/-, Rag2-/-Il2rg-/-, Cxcr6-/- and Cxcr6gfp/gfp, Cxcr3-/-, Tbx21-/-, Nfil3-/-, Il15ra-/-, Gata3fl/fl-Vav-Cre, CD45.1/CD45.2 congenics. Human only for the tissue-residency arm (Cuff 2016: liver transplant donor/recipient pairs; Marquardt 2015 PMID 25672754; Stegmann 2016 PMID 27210614).
what_was_measured: In mouse, in vivo, hepatic mononuclear cells were prepared by 40-um filtration + Nycodenz gradient from hapten- or virus-sensitized donors, sorted on the gate CD45+ NK1.1+ CD3-/TCR- (Paust 2010) and 8x10^4 cells transferred i.v. into naive Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients; readout at 24-48 h was ear-swelling (caliper, micrometres) after DNFB or oxazolone challenge, and separately survival curves after lethal homologous vs heterologous influenza/VSV challenge, in n=8-10 recipient mice per group. In mouse, in vivo, liver CD3-CD19-CD122+ cells were split into CD49a+DX5- vs CD49a-DX5+ and 8x10^4 sorted cells from OXA-sensitized donors were transferred into naive B6, challenged 1 month later, ear-swelling readout, n=4 mice per group; in parallel CD45.1/CD45.2 parabionts were joined for 14 days and allotype composition of each liver subset was scored in 7 parabiotic pairs (Peng 2013), and 14-day parabiosis with the same readout in 8 pairs across two experiments (Sojka 2014). In mouse, in vivo, at 1 month post-sensitization, 5x10^4 cells sorted as CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+CD49a+IL-7Ra+ (ILC1), IL-7Ra- CD49a+ (LrNK) or cNK from OXA-sensitized Rag1-/- donors were transferred into naive recipients and ear thickness measured every 24 h, n=4-6 mice per group (Wang 2018). In human, ex vivo, donor- vs recipient-origin leukocytes were discriminated by anti-HLA-A2/A3 staining of perfusate, biopsy and explant from 7 HLA-mismatched liver transplants plus 5 re-transplant explants (longest interval 13 years), scoring Eomes, T-bet, CXCR6, CD69, CD49a, CD56, CD16 by flow; plus a 7-day IL-15 +/- IL-12 +/- TGF-b culture of sorted Eomes-lo NK cells scoring Eomes upregulation (Cuff 2016).
n: O'Leary 2006 (primary): NOT VERIFIABLE, methods paywalled. Paust 2010: n=8-10 recipient mice per group. Peng 2013: n=4 mice per group for the CHS adoptive transfer; 7 parabiotic pairs; syngeneic/mixed BM chimeras 10^6 cells per arm. Sojka 2014: 8 parabiotic pairs total (2 independent experiments x 4 pairs). Wang 2018: n=4-6 mice per group. Cuff 2016: 7 HLA-mismatched liver transplant donor/recipient pairs + 5 re-transplant explants.
n_unit: mice per group (adoptive-transfer recipients); parabiotic mouse pairs; human liver-transplant donor/recipient pairs. NOT cells — the 8x10^4 / 5x10^4 / 10^6 figures are transferred cell doses, not n.
controls: Paust 2010: mock (no-cell) recipients of Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- confirmed absent NK1.1+ cells; splenic and naive-donor NK cells as non-memory transfer controls; challenge with a non-sensitizing hapten and with a heterologous virus as antigen-specificity controls; Cxcr6-/- donors as the genetic arm. Peng 2013: paired CD49a- DX5+ liver subset transferred in parallel as the internal negative control; congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 allotype discrimination in parabionts; syngeneic BM transplant to test bone-marrow origin. Sojka 2014: circulating CD49a-DX5+ subset in the same parabiont as the internal equilibration control; Tbx21-/-, Nfil3-/-, Il15ra-/- as genetic requirement controls. Wang 2018: three sorted populations (cNK, IL-7Ra- LrNK, IL-7Ra+ ILC1, all >=95% purity) transferred side-by-side from the same donors — this is the only design in the chain that can actually attribute memory to one of the three. Cuff 2016: non-transplanted liver perfusate and paired pre-/post-transplant biopsies. MISSING THROUGHOUT: no clonal barcoding, no Cre-lox fate map, no live imaging of a single cell acquiring the memory state; no experiment in which a purified naive cell of defined lineage is followed to a memory cell.
strongest_alternative_explanation: The claim splits into two parts that carry very different evidential weight, and the weak half is the one the label "NK" sits on. (1) EXISTENCE of a transferable, antigen-specific, liver-restricted memory population in T/B-deficient mice is genuinely supported by OBS_TRANSFER, replicated in four labs. (2) The ORIGIN/IDENTITY as "NK cell" is only INF_MARKER, and the marker panel used to establish it is provably incapable of the distinction: Paust 2010 gated CD45+NK1.1+CD3-/TCR- with NO CD49a and NO DX5, a gate that pools conventional NK cells and liver ILC1s. The strongest alternative is therefore an ENTITY MISASSIGNMENT rather than a false transition: the memory-mediating cell is a pre-existing, tissue-resident, Eomes- T-bet+ CD49a+DX5- IL-7Ra+ ILC1 that was never a conventional NK cell and never "became" anything — it was simply present in the liver, selected/expanded by sensitization, and mis-gated as NK. This is exactly the canonical "pre-existing subset selected rather than converted" alternative, and it is the one the data now favour: Wang 2018, sorting cNK vs IL-7Ra- LrNK vs IL-7Ra+ ILC1 from the same donors, found ONLY the IL-7Ra+ CD49a+ ILC1 fraction conferred hapten recall; Klose 2014 showed that NKp46+IL-7Ra+ T-bet-dependent lineage arises from the Id2+ CHILP, which explicitly does NOT give rise to cNK; Sojka 2014 showed the CD49a+DX5- liver cells stay host-restricted across 14-day parabiosis and are Eomes-negative. A second, independent alternative applies to the ORIGIN sub-claim specifically: Peng 2013's assertion that these cells derive from hepatic HPC/HSC rather than bone marrow rests on a BM-chimera reconstitution deficit ("less than 15% DX5- NK cells"), which is equally explained by failure of a radioresistant resident population to be replaced under irradiation — i.e. residency/radioresistance, not local hepatic ontogeny — and is superseded by the CHILP-origin result. A third alternative is a species artefact in the human extrapolation: the human liver-resident population is T-bet-lo Eomes-HI (Cuff 2016; Stegmann 2016), the OPPOSITE transcription-factor polarity to the mouse T-bet-hi Eomes-NEGATIVE ILC1, so "liver memory NK cell" in mouse and "liver-resident NK cell" in human are not the same entity and the mouse ILC1 reassignment does not transfer.
counter_evidence: [audit] FOUND, and it is decisive for the identity half of the claim. (a) Peng 2013 (JCI, PMID 23524967) — with Sojka and Yokoyama as co-authors — opens by conceding "the phenotype and origin of these 'memory' NK cells cannot be distinguished from other NK cell subpopulations", then localises the memory to CD49a+DX5- cells whose microarray shows Eomes "expressed at much higher levels in DX5+ NK cells", i.e. the memory-bearing subset is Eomes-low. (b) Sojka 2014 (eLife, PMID 24714492): 14-day parabiosis, 8 pairs — "Host CD49a+DX5- NK cells were primarily found in the indicated host tissue" while "CD49a-DX5+ NK cells of both allotypes were found in both parabionts"; combined with Tbx21-/-, Nfil3-/-, Il15ra-/- requirements this defines them as a lineage distinct from thymic and conventional splenic NK. (c) Daussy 2014 (JEM, PMID 24516120): T-bet and Eomes instruct two distinct liver vs bone-marrow group-1 lineages. (d) Klose 2014 (Cell, PMID 24725403) is the hardest ontogeny counter-evidence: the Id2+ CHILP "differentiated into ILC2 and ILC3 lineages, but not into conventional natural killer (cNK) cells", instead giving rise to "a peculiar NKp46+ IL-7Ra+ ILC lineage that required T-bet for specification and was distinct of cNK cells" — so the cell now credited with liver hapten memory does not descend from the NK progenitor at all. (e) Wang 2018 (Nat Commun, PMID 30451860), from Tian/Peng's own group, transfers the memory function outright: "LN IL-7Ra+ ILC1s, rather than IL-7Ra- cNK cells, conferred long-term recall responses", with the memory cells T-bet+Eomes-; note also that the "novel lineage-tracing model" phrasing in the preprint/press title is not supported by its methods, which list no reporter or Cre strain, only CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic transfer. (f) Cell Rep 2024 (PMID 38363684) continues the reassignment, framing the population as RORa-dependent ILC1s. (g) Contemporaneous ADMISSION from the pro-NK camp: J Immunol 2025 (PMID 40381992), which re-tests O'Leary's Ly49C-I claim, states outright that "the current known markers of memory NK cells cannot adequately discriminate between conventional NK cells and memory NK cells, making this question difficult to answer" and concedes the memory population may be "a distinct ILC subset" — as of 2025 the founding lab's lineage does not claim the entity is resolved. (h) Human counter-evidence to a direct mouse-to-human read-across: Cuff 2016 (PMID 27798170) shows human liver-resident NK are T-bet-lo Eomes-HI, retained up to 13 years, yet "can be recruited from the circulation during adult life", with sorted Eomes-lo cells upregulating Eomes in 7-day IL-15/IL-12/TGF-b culture — a residency + in vitro conversion result of the opposite TF polarity to mouse ILC1. NOT FOUND, distinguished from does-not-exist: I searched specifically for a failure-to-replicate or artefact critique of the hapten-CHS memory phenomenon itself ("NK cell memory hapten controversy failed reproduce"; "contact hypersensitivity Rag deficient mice B-1 cells exosomes hapten specific antibody Askenase") and read no such paper — I record this as a search run with nothing found, NOT as evidence that no such critique exists. || [adversarial] SIX items the row missed, four of which point AWAY from the row's confident ILC1 reassignment and toward the canonical "pre-existing subset selected, not converted" alternative. (1) THE DECISIVE SELECTION-NOT-CONVERSION EXPERIMENT IS INSIDE THE ROW'S OWN BEST-CONTROLLED PAPER AND THE ROW DOES NOT REPORT IT. Wang 2018 (PMID 30451860 / PMC6242895), Supplementary Fig. 5c,d, verbatim from the archived full text: "naive CD45.2+ splenic cNK cells were transferred into naive CD45.1 mice. Upon hapten sensitization, donor cells in recipient LNs did not acquire IL-7Ra and CD49a expression, maintaining their cNK cell phenotype, suggesting that cNK cells did not convert into ILC1s in the CHS model." A congenic transfer purpose-built to test the conversion, returning a NEGATIVE. This is the single strongest piece of evidence in the whole chain that no cNK -> memory-ILC1 conversion occurs. (2) WANG 2018'S OWN KINETICS SAY REDISTRIBUTION, NOT CONVERSION AND NOT CLONAL EXPANSION: Ki67 unchanged when LN ILC1 numbers peak ("suggesting that the increase of IL-7Ra+ ILC1s was not due to clonal expansion"); the liver increase "may be a consequence of cell migration, rather than local proliferation"; contraction with no rise in 7AAD+ apoptosis, i.e. egress; recruitment CXCR3-dependent and abolished in Cxcr3-/-; egress S1PR1/FTY720-sensitive; the whole liver memory increase abrogated by lymphadenectomy or LTbR-Ig-induced LN deficiency. So "memory formation" here is trafficking of a standing pool along an LN-liver axis — textbook selection/redistribution of a pre-existing subset. (3) WANG 2018'S PARABIOSIS CONTRADICTS THE ROW'S "RESIDENT THEREFORE SEPARATE LINEAGE" READING OF SOJKA 2014: CD45.1/CD45.2 parabionts, 2 weeks, then OXA — "donor-derived ILC1s increased up to 30%" and the authors "conclude that LN ILC1s may be partially recruited from blood." (4) INDEPENDENT REPLICATION THE ROW NEITHER FOUND NOR CREDITED: van den Boorn JG, ..., Garbi N, Hartmann G, Hornung V. "Inflammasome-Dependent Induction of Adaptive NK Cell Memory." Immunity 2016;44:1406-21, PMID 27287410 (Bonn/LMU — independent of both von Andrian and Tian/Peng). Monobenzone pro-hapten; long-lasting melanocyte-specific response, NK-dependent, "fully intact in the absence of T- and B cells"; memory NK "resided in the liver and transfer of these cells conferred melanocyte-specific immunity to naive animals"; abolished by macrophage depletion or loss of NLRP3, ASC or IL-18. This is a third independent lab and it STRENGTHENS the existence half. CAVEAT (G1): I have abstract only (archived P3_27287410.txt); I did NOT read its methods. (5) THE ROW'S ONTOGENY VERDICT IS OUT OF DATE AND POINTS THE WRONG WAY. The row states Peng 2013's hepatic-HPC/HSC origin claim "is directly contradicted by Klose 2014's CHILP-origin result". Bai L, ..., Vivier E, Peng H, Sun R, Tian Z. "Liver type 1 innate lymphoid cells develop locally via an interferon-g-dependent loop." Science 2021;371:eaba4177, PMID 33766856: adult mouse liver contains fetal-liver-derived Lin-Sca-1+Mac-1+ HSCs, "includes Lin-CD122+CD49a+ progenitors that can generate liver ILC1s but not conventional natural killer cells", with IFN-g from the ILC1s themselves driving development in situ. That REHABILITATES local hepatic origin rather than refuting it, and it is not in conflict with a CHILP-type progenitor being resident in liver. CAVEAT (G1): Science is paywalled and there is no PMC deposit; WebFetch on science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aba4177 returned HTTP 403. I have ABSTRACT ONLY and did not read its methods — I record it as a pointer, not as verified methods. (6) NK<->ILC1 IS A DEMONSTRATED PLASTIC AXIS, SO THE ROW'S MARKER-BASED REASSIGNMENT IS NOT LICENSED EITHER. Gao Y et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004, PMID 28759001: "TGF-b-signaling-dependent conversion of NK cells (CD49a-CD49b+Eomes+) into intermediate type 1 innate lymphoid cell (intILC1) (CD49a+CD49b+Eomes+) populations and ILC1 (CD49a+CD49b-Eomes-int) populations in the tumor microenvironment." Cortez VS et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:995, PMID 28759002: Smad4-deficient NK cells "unexpectedly acquired an ILC1-like gene signature". Cortez VS et al., Immunity 2016;44:1127, PMID 27156386: TGF-b imprints the salivary-gland ILC1 program. CD49a+ DX5- Eomes-low is therefore a TGF-b-INDUCIBLE STATE, and "CD49a+DX5-, therefore never a cNK" is a non-sequitur. Note items (1) and (6) cut in opposite directions: together they mean the identity question is genuinely OPEN, not settled toward ILC1 as the row asserts. (7) SELECTION OF A PRE-EXISTING GERMLINE-RECEPTOR SUBSET IS WHAT THE FIELD'S STRONGEST DATA ACTUALLY SHOW. Sun 2009: expansion is confined to the pre-existing Ly49H+ subset and is abolished with MCMV-Dm157. Flommersfeld 2021: no bipotent clones — "progeny derived from single Ly49H+ NK cells showed limited diversification and instead adopted one of two distinct fates", i.e. fate was already fixed in the transferred cell. And PMID 40381992 (J Immunol 2025) — note its title is "Ly49G, but NOT Ly49C/I, is dispensable for diverse antigen-specific memory NK cell responses", i.e. Ly49C/I remains REQUIRED, replicating O'Leary 2006 nineteen years on, by antibody depletion of a STANDING receptor-defined subset. Selection, not conversion, on every design. NO failed-replication paper found. NOT_SEARCHED BY ME: the Askenase B-1-cell/exosome CHS alternative-effector literature (the row claims to have run it with zero hits; I did not re-run it). crossfield_g4_findings: The mechanism's home field is TISSUE RESIDENCY (TRM), and it invalidates the two assays this claim's origin half rests on. LESSON 1 — PARABIOSIS IS A RESIDENCY ASSAY, NOT AN ONTOGENY ASSAY. Masopust D et al., J Exp Med 2010;207:553, PMID 20156972 / PMC2839151 (fetched and read; lit.py methods body truncated to 759 chars, recovered by WebFetch): their own residency evidence is intestinal TRANSPLANTATION (42 d post-transplant, minimal recirculation of host memory into graft) plus FTY720 (no reduction in TRM after 30 d); the parabiosis result is CITED from Klonowski KD et al., Immunity 2004;20:551-62, PMID 15142524, not performed. The canonical TRM is a cell that circulated, entered tissue, and then stopped recirculating. Non-equilibration in a 14-day parabiosis is EXACTLY what a converted-then-resident cell looks like. Therefore Peng 2013 (14 d, 7 pairs), Sojka 2014 (14 d, 8 pairs) and Wang 2018 (2 wk) cannot distinguish "separate lineage" from "circulating cell that converted and then stopped recirculating" — and the audited row repeats that category error by listing Sojka's parabiosis as counter-evidence (b) for a lineage claim. Same for Cuff 2016's human transplant chimerism (7 HLA-mismatched pairs + 5 explants): donor persistence proves retention, not separate ontogeny, and Cuff itself reports the cells "can be recruited from the circulation during adult life". LESSON 2 — IN THE HOME FIELD, CIRCULATING -> RESIDENT CONVERSION IS THE DEFAULT, AND IT IS DRIVEN BY THE SAME TWO CYTOKINES. Mackay LK et al., Nat Immunol 2013;14:1294, PMID 24162776: CD103+CD8+ skin TRM "developed in the skin from epithelium-infiltrating precursor cells that lacked expression of the effector-cell marker KLRG1"; "a combination of entry into the epithelium plus local signaling by interleukin 15 (IL-15) and transforming growth factor-b (TGF-b) was required"; differentiation "resulted in the progressive acquisition of a unique transcriptional profile that differed from that of circulating memory cells". So a divergent transcriptome + integrin/retention markers + parabiosis non-equilibration is the EXPECTED signature of a CONVERTED resident cell. Sojka 2014's and Daussy 2014's inference from precisely that triad to "distinct lineage" is not licensed by home-field standards, and neither the original papers nor the audited row flags it. The convergence is exact: IL-15 (Il15ra-/- requirement in Sojka) and TGF-b (Cortez 2016/2017 PMIDs 27156386/28759002; Gao 2017 PMID 28759001) are the same two signals that install CD49a and extinguish Eomes in group-1 ILCs. LESSON 3 — RESIDENCY IS AN INSTRUCTED TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROGRAM SHARED ACROSS UNRELATED LINEAGES, SO ITS MARKERS CANNOT BE LINEAGE MARKERS. Mackay LK et al., Science 2016;352:459, PMID 27102484: Hobit + Blimp1 "mediate the development of Trm cells in skin, gut, liver, and kidney" and the same module "is also required for other populations of tissue-resident lymphocytes, including natural killer T (NKT) cells and liver-resident NK cells, all of which share a common transcriptional program." This is OBS_GENETIC evidence, in the home field, that the liver CD49a+/CD69+/Eomes-low "resident NK" signature is a program running across at least three unrelated lineages. Using it to assign ontogeny — which is what the entire CD49a+DX5- reassignment does — is a marker-similarity inference, INF_MARKER, exactly as the row concluded but for a reason stronger than the row gives. LESSON 4 — EVEN IN THE ILC HOME FIELD, "RESIDENT" DOES NOT MEAN "CLOSED LINEAGE". Gasteiger G, Fan X, Dikiy S, Lee SY, Rudensky AY. Science 2015;350:981, PMID 26472762: ILCs are tissue-resident and locally self-renewing, BUT "at later time points after infection, cells from hematogenous sources helped to partially replenish the pool of resident ILCs." Wang 2018's own 30% donor-derived LN ILC1 in parabionts after sensitization reproduces this. LESSON 5 — A GATING ARTEFACT FROM THE T-CELL FIELD THAT NONE OF THESE PAPERS CONTROLLED. Anderson KG, ..., Masopust D. "Intravascular staining for discrimination of vascular and tissue leukocytes." Nat Protoc 2014;9:209, PMID 24385150. Intravenous anti-CD45 labelling minutes before harvest is required to separate vascular from parenchymal leukocytes; tissue digests conflate them. The liver is a sinusoidal organ in which a large fraction of "hepatic mononuclear cells" are intravascular. Paust 2010 used 40-um filtration + density gradient; Peng 2013 and Wang 2018 used Percoll interface; none used an i.v. label. So "hepatic NK cell" in the founding papers is an ANATOMICAL-PREPARATION category, not a verified parenchymal-residency category — an artefact route the audited row never considers, and one that also weakens the liver-vs-spleen contrast on which the whole "liver-restricted memory" claim turns. LESSON 6 — MYELOID/TRAINED IMMUNITY: INNATE MEMORY CAN BE WRITTEN AT THE PROGENITOR LEVEL. Kaufmann E et al., "BCG Educates Hematopoietic Stem Cells to Generate Protective Innate Immunity against Tuberculosis." Cell 2018;172:176, PMID 29328912. Central trained immunity means a recall phenotype can be encoded in progenitors and read out in a mature effector that never itself met the antigen. Applied here: the transferred hepatic population's recall could reflect an imprint on hepatic progenitors — which Bai 2021 (PMID 33766856, abstract only) says exist in adult liver — rather than a memory state in the transferred mature cell. No paper in the P3 chain excludes this: none transferred progenitors, none profiled progenitor epigenetics, and the hapten transfers use bulk sorted populations at >=95% purity, which still leaves up to 5% contaminant in a functional-only readout. NET EFFECT ON THE CLAIM: the home fields do NOT rescue the "NK" label — they make the identity question harder, because CD49a/Eomes-low/parabiosis-non-equilibration are all residency-program readouts rather than ontogeny readouts. But they also refute the audited row's confident settlement toward ILC1, because the same literature shows the ILC1 phenotype is TGF-b-inducible from cNK. What survives is: a transferable, antigen-specific, liver-restricted memory unit exists (three independent labs); its lineage label is unmeasured; and the only clean conversion test ever run in the CHS model (Wang 2018 Supp. Fig. 5c,d) came back negative, favouring selection of a pre-existing subset over conversion.

what_was_measured: In humans, dNK were isolated from first-trimester decidua basalis obtained at elective abortion (gestational age never stated in the paper), enriched by immunomagnetic depletion of CD3+ and CD16+ cells and further purified with anti-CD56 beads; at the fresh timepoint (t=0, immediately after tissue digestion and bead purification) and after 36 h of culture in 12 ng/ml IL-15 in RPMI-1640 + 10% FCS, specific lysis of 51Cr-labelled 721.221 and K562 target cells was measured in 4-h chromium-release assays across graded E:T ratios, against autologous-preparation fresh dNK and against peripheral-blood NK; in parallel, at 20 min of conjugation, the percentage of dNK-721.221 conjugates showing MTOC (alpha/gamma-tubulin) and perforin-granule polarization toward the contact site, and the percentage showing CD2 / LFA-1 / F-actin accumulation at the contact site, were scored by confocal microscopy on at least 50 conjugates per slide. n = 4 independent decidual preparations for the fresh dNK vs pNK lysis comparison, n = 3 for the 36-h IL-15 arm (one shown as representative), and at least 3 for every polarization percentage. Readouts: % specific 51Cr release; % conjugates with polarized MTOC/perforin (fresh dNK 19%, IL-15-cultured dNK 66%, pNK 55%, YTS 74%).
n: 3 (IL-15 rescue arm, the load-bearing experiment); 4 (fresh dNK vs pNK lysis); >=3 (each polarization percentage). Counter-source Siewiera 2013: 10.
n_unit: independent decidual preparations, each from a separate first-trimester elective termination (the paper says only "independent experiments" and never states a donor count, gestational age, or purity figure; unit inferred from "dNK from the same preparation"). MISSING, and material to the claim: (1) no 36-h medium-only / no-cytokine culture arm — the comparison is fresh (t=0) vs 36 h + IL-15, so time in culture and removal from decidual tissue are fully confounded with the cytokine; (2) no IL-15 dose-response and no anti-IL-15 or IL-15Ra blockade; (3) no post-culture purity, viability, count or division tracking, so preferential survival/outgrowth of a minority already-competent cell is not excluded; (4) IL-18 was never tested by Kopcow at all; (5) no donor-level statistics (representative experiment shown for the rescue).
strongest_alternative_explanation: The 36-h ex vivo culture, not IL-15, does the work — and the paper itself offers this. Kopcow's own Discussion states the alternative verbatim: "the immunosuppressive environment of the decidua might be responsible for blocking MTOC and granule polarization. Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment, for example, by in vitro incubation in the presence of IL-15." Because there is no 36-h medium-only arm, nothing in the data separates "IL-15 signals a state change" from "release from tissue-imposed suppression plus 36 h of recovery from collagenase digestion and bead handling". Second, non-exclusive alternative: selection rather than conversion — IL-15 is a survival/proliferation factor for CD56bright NK, no purity, count, viability or division tracking was done after culture, and the starting population is only bead-enriched (CD3/CD16 depletion does not exclude a CD16-neg-but-competent or contaminating minority), so preferential survival/expansion of an already-cytotoxic minority reproduces both the lysis curve and the 19%->66% polarization shift without any single cell changing state. Third (G4, mechanism's home field): the entire phenotype is generic to freshly isolated tissue lymphocytes, not specific to decidual identity — CD8+ tumour-infiltrating T cells are nonlytic immediately on isolation despite full perforin/granzyme granule content, with the same defect in MTOC mobilization and lytic granule exocytosis (Radoja/Frey, PMID 11673513, cited by Kopcow as ref 27), and TIL effector function is likewise restored by ex vivo gamma-c cytokine culture (e.g. IL-2, PMC2377057). A result that reproduces in TILs, CD8 T cells and dNK alike is evidence about ex vivo culture of tissue lymphocytes, not about a dNK-specific licensing switch. Fourth, the baseline is not zero: fresh dNK already lysed at ~15% of pNK levels and already polarized granules in 19-22% of conjugates, so the effect is a quantitative increase from a non-zero baseline, not the flipping of an off switch.

The specific IL-15+IL-18 combination named in the claim is the one combination reported NOT to work; the working partner for IL-18 was IL-12. (Abstract only — see fulltext field.) Note also its readout was bulk decidual lymphocytes, not purified dNK. (2) NO CYTOKINE IS REQUIRED AT ALL: El Costa 2008 (PMID 18713971) reports that in FRESH, uncultured dNK, mAb engagement of NKp46 (and to a lesser extent NKG2C, but not NKp30) induced calcium mobilization, perforin polarization, granule exocytosis and efficient target lysis — no IL-15, no IL-18, no culture period. (Abstract only.) (3) Siewiera 2013 (PMID 23592985, PMC3617138, FULL TEXT READ): fresh dNK purified from 8-12 wk decidua basalis killed autologous HCMV-infected decidual fibroblasts in 18-h 51Cr assays, reaching ~75% specific lysis at E:T 50 with no killing of uninfected autologous fibroblasts, confirmed across "a cohort of 10 decidua basalis"; 83+/-4% of dNK synapses with infected targets showed polarized perforin granules vs 28% with uninfected targets, and CD107a degranulation rose from 6 h. crossfield_g4_findings: The mechanism's home field does not merely fail to support R1 — it says the specific readout R1 asserts is the one that does NOT durably change, and that R1's experimental design cannot distinguish reprogramming from acute activation. A. NK'S OWN HOME FIELD FOR THIS EXACT MANIPULATION IS CYTOKINE-INDUCED MEMORY-LIKE (CIML) NK, AND ITS RESULT CUTS AGAINST R1. Cooper 2009 (PMID 19181844, PNAS, mouse, abstract only): NK preactivated with IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 were adoptively transferred into naive hosts and congenically re-identified 7-22 days later. They "produce significantly more IFN-gamma when restimulated. This memory-like property is intrinsic to the NK cell. By contrast, memory-like NK cells DO NOT EXPRESS GRANZYME B PROTEIN AND KILL TARGETS SIMILARLY TO NAIVE NK CELLS." This is an OBS_TRANSFER-grade in vivo test of a cytokine-induced NK functional state change, and it separates the two readouts cleanly: IFN-gamma persists, cytotoxicity does not. Romee 2016 (PMID 27655849, Sci Transl Med, human, abstract only) establishes the design standard: "differentiate after a brief preactivation with IL-12, IL-15, and IL-18 and exhibit enhanced responses to cytokine or activating receptor RESTIMULATION for WEEKS TO MONTHS AFTER preactivation." Two consequences for R1: (i) the replicated cocktail is IL-12+IL-15+IL-18, so the claim's bare "IL-15/IL-18" is plausibly a garbled CIML protocol — and Tokmadzic 2002 independently found IL-12, not IL-15, to be IL-18's working partner on decidual lymphocytes; (ii) Kopcow measured dNK at the end of 36 h of CONTINUOUS IL-15 exposure with no washout, no rest and no re-challenge, so his result is by construction an acute-activation measurement, not a demonstration that any state changed. B. THE uNK FIELD'S OWN TRAINED-IMMUNITY RESULT AGREES, AND IT IS ALREADY IN THIS REGISTRY AS R4. Gamliel 2018 (PMID 29768178, Immunity, abstract only): Pregnancy-Trained decidual NK from repeated pregnancies carry "a unique transcriptome and epigenetic signature" with "open chromatin around the enhancers of IFNG and VEGFA," and activation yields increased IFN-gamma and VEGF-alpha. The epigenetically encoded, persisting uNK program is cytokine/growth-factor secretion. Cytotoxicity is again not the trained axis. C. T-CELL EXHAUSTION: FUNCTIONAL RESCUE MEASURED UNDER CONTINUING STIMULUS IS THE FIELD'S CANONICAL FALSE POSITIVE. Pauken 2016 (PMID 27789795, Science, mouse, abstract only): PD-L1 blockade reinvigorates exhausted CD8 T cells transcriptionally, but their epigenetic profile "was minimally remodeled after PD-L1 blockade"; reinvigorated cells "became reexhausted if antigen concentration remained high and failed to become T MEM upon antigen clearance" — "epigenetic fate inflexibility may limit current immunotherapies." Sen 2016 (PMID 27789799, Science) maps the exhaustion-specific enhancer landscape. claim_text: Tumour NK dysfunction reversible vs fixed
species: Primary source: mouse (C57BL/6J; congenic Ly5a x C57BL/6J for CD45.1/CD45.2 discrimination; Prf1-/- in supporting arms). Counter-source: human (healthy adult volunteer PBMC-derived NK cells for the in vitro arm; HCC / liver-metastasis patients for the ex vivo arm).
what_was_measured: In C57BL/6J mice injected i.v. with 5x10^7 RMA-KR lymphoma cells (RMA CRISPR-edited to B2m-KO and lentivirally transduced with the NKG2D ligand Rae1-beta, i.e. an MHC-I-negative, NK-activating disseminated lymphoma), at late-stage tumour growth, splenic NK cells were FACS-sorted and adoptively transferred via the retro-orbital sinus into tumour-free congenic Ly5a x C57BL/6J recipients; 7 to 13 days after transfer donor-derived NK cells were re-purified from recipients (donor vs recipient discriminated by CD45.2 versus CD45.1-CD45.2 alleles) and assayed by flow cytometry for (a) surface Lag-3, CD73 and Tim-3 and (b) co-expression of CD107a and IFN-gamma after plate-bound anti-NK1.1 crosslinking or cytokine restimulation, in n = 10 to 15 mice per group (n = 3 to 12 for the ICP heatmap panel). In the same study, in vitro, NK cells sorted from RMA-KR-bearing mice at late-stage tumour growth were cultured with IL-15 or IL-21 and assayed for viability and for CD107a/IFN-gamma after NK1.1 stimulation, in n = 3 to 18 mice per group; and in vivo, RMA-KR-bearing mice received 2 doses of 4 ug IL-15/IL-15Ralpha complex i.p. 2 days apart with NK function assayed the day after the second dose. In the counter-source, human NK cells enriched from healthy-donor PBMC were cultured in IL-15 (50 ng/mL) +/- TGF-beta (10 ng/mL) for short-term versus a 17-day prolonged setup, TGF-beta was withdrawn by a single PBS wash into fresh medium, and chromatin accessibility (bulk ATAC-seq), transcription (bulk RNA-seq, 5 biological replicates per condition), H3K4me3/H3K27ac/CTCF occupancy (CUT&RUN, 250,000-500,000 sorted cells per reaction) and killing of BxPC-3 PDAC targets (xCELLigence impedance, 1:1 E:T, 48 h) were measured after withdrawal.
n: Primary source, key reversal-by-transfer experiment: n = 10 to 15 mice per group (function panel), n = 3 to 12 mice per group (ICP panel). Primary source, in vitro cytokine rescue of sorted dysfunctional NK cells: n = 3 to 18 mice per group. Counter-source: 5 biological replicates (healthy donors) per condition for RNA-seq; donor/patient numbers for ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN and the HCC cohort are not stated numerically anywhere in the preprint Methods (killing assay stated only as "at least duplicate").
n_unit: mice (primary source; NOT cells — sorted NK pools were per-mouse and group sizes are stated per mouse in the figure legends); donors/patients (counter-source)
controls: Primary source: (i) tumour-free control-mouse NK cells sorted and transferred in parallel through the identical pipeline; (ii) a second tumour arm, parental RMA (MHC-I+, non-NK-activating), which induced ICPs but NOT dysfunction — this dissociates tumour burden from dysfunction; (iii) pre-transfer baseline measured on the same sorted populations ("analyzed before and after transfer"); (iv) an explicit anti-selection control — frequency of NK cells recovered from the RMA-KR condition was compared with control and reported as "in the same order of magnitude" (fig. S7C); (v) depletion/blockade specificity controls (200 ug polyclonal anti-rat IgG isotype; depletion confirmed with antibody clones different from those used to deplete); (vi) IgG2a isotype for plate-bound stimulation. Stated methodological weaknesses, verbatim: "The number of mice used in each experiment was not power-calculated, given the large number of questions asked"; "No randomization was performed, with the exception of experiments in which animal survival was monitored"; "data from mice in which tumors had not grown were excluded." Counter-source controls: IL-15-only cultures matched for time, and continuous-TGF-beta versus withdrawal arms; the authors themselves flag the confound that "NK cells were maintained in IL-15 for prolonged culture periods, and long-term IL-15 exposure itself has been reported to induce transcriptional and epigenetic adaptations."
strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION, NOT PER-CELL REVERSION. Over the 7-13 days the sorted NK cells spend in the tumour-free congenic host, a residual functional minority could preferentially survive and/or proliferate (the host is IL-15-replete and NK turnover is fast on that timescale), so the recovered CD45.2 population need not be the same cells that were dysfunctional at sort. The paper's only guard against this is a frequency argument — recovered NK numbers were "in the same order of magnitude" as control (fig. S7C) — with no proliferation dye in that particular experiment (CTV was used in the transfer-INTO-tumour experiments, not the transfer-OUT-of-tumour recovery experiment), no clonal or per-cell tracking, and no barcoding. SECOND, AND MORE IMPORTANT FOR THE CLAIM AS WORDED: the lesion this paper demonstrates and then reverses is a proximal-signalling one — impaired Akt/Erk/S6 phosphorylation with normal STAT5, and reduced CD122 internalisation, i.e. an mTORC1-level defect — and a signalling-level state is close to definitionally reversible once the engaging ligand is withdrawn. The study performs NO chromatin, methylation or ATAC readout at any point, so it cannot exclude a stable epigenetic program at effector loci coexisting with recovered CD107a/IFN-gamma. THIRD, SCOPE: RMA-KR is a disseminated MHC-I-null lymphoma read out in spleen; the "dysfunctional" cells are splenic NK cells from a tumour-bearing animal, not NK cells dissected out of a solid-tumour mass, so generalisation to the solid-tumour TME that the R2 wording invokes is an extrapolation. For the counter-source, the mirror-image alternative is that 17 days of continuous high-dose IL-15 plus TGF-beta in a 96-well plate drives terminal differentiation/senescence or culture exhaustion, and that the HCC ATAC signal is measured on PERIPHERAL BLOOD NK cells cross-sectionally, which cannot distinguish an imprint acquired in the tumour and carried out of it from a systemic effect on NK cells that never entered the tumour, or from a shift in CD56bright/CD56dim composition between patients and controls.
counter_evidence: [audit] FOUND, and it materially changes the picture. It is however NOT peer-reviewed, and its irreversibility demonstration is entirely in vitro on healthy-donor NK cells with recombinant TGF-beta; no tumour-derived NK cell is ever subjected to a withdrawal experiment. (2) Within the primary source itself there is internal counter-evidence to naive reversibility: "Ex vivo blockade of ICPs in cultures of total splenocytes from RMA-KR-bearing mice did not restore NK cell responsiveness, even when several ICPs were targeted," and in vivo Tim-3 or Lag-3 blockade improved neither survival nor NK function; and high-dose IL-15 in vitro improved but did not fully normalise dysfunctional NK reactivity ("a difference with control NK cells persisted, suggesting that other signals were necessary to fully revert dysfunction"). The claim R2 actually asserts - that the cells which were dysfunctional reverted - is not observed. No cell is assayed twice; "before" is an aliquot of the sorted donor pool, "after" is cells harvested from different (recipient) animals. The bridge between the two is carried entirely by fig. S7C, whose full argument is: "This was unlikely due to the selection of a small functional population because the frequency of NK cells recovered from the RMA-KR condition was in the same order of magnitude as that of the control condition." That is a population-frequency comparison BETWEEN DIFFERENT RECIPIENT MICE credited as evidence that the same cells persisted - precisely the pattern flagged in the re-examination brief, and it is INF_KINETIC/INF_MARKER grade, not observation grade. "Same order of magnitude" also tolerates a ~5-fold loss, and a frequency argument is structurally blind to the scenario that matters (minority survives and proliferates to refill the niche). crossfield_g4_findings: THE T-CELL EXHAUSTION FIELD HAS ALREADY RUN THIS EXACT EXPERIMENT AND REACHED THE OPPOSITE CONCLUSION. (A) PHILIP 2017, Nature 545:452, PMID 28514453 (full text archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_G4_PMC5693219.txt) is the decisive item and is the direct methodological template for PMID 39196934. Verbatim from the Results: "when we re-isolated TCR-TAG from liver lesions and cultured them in vitro with IL15... L5 and L7 regained the ability to produce IFNg and TNFa, but TCR-TAG isolated at day 12 and after did not. Thus state 1 dysfunction is plastic, but with further chromatin remodeling between days 7 and 14, becomes fixed (state 2)." Three consequences for R2. (i) REVERSIBILITY IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE STATE, IT IS A FUNCTION OF EXPOSURE DURATION. RMA-KR is a fast disseminated lymphoma; dysfunction appears within 16 h and mice are at end stage around days 12-14, so the sorted "late-stage" NK cells have had at most ~1-2 weeks of signal. In Philip's frame that samples the plastic window and cannot exclude a fixed state that the model never reaches. The claim as worded ("reversible versus fixed") is therefore likely a false dichotomy, and PMID 39196934 cannot resolve it because its model has no long-exposure arm. Strikingly, the counter-source preprint's own exposure is also 7 days — precisely the boundary. (ii) THE ICP RESULT IS NOT NOVEL AND THE ICP-LOSS READOUT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF REVERSION: "PD1 and LAG3 were similarly expressed by both plastic (L5, L7) and fixed (L14+) dysfunctional TST and thus not informative in this regard." PMID 39196934 uses loss of Lag-3/CD73/Tim-3 after transfer as part of its reversion evidence; the T-cell field established that those markers do not track the plastic/fixed axis. (iii) THE SELECTION ALTERNATIVE IS EMPIRICAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Philip sorted heterogeneous day-14 populations by CD38/CD101: "While CD38lo/CD101lo-L14 regained the ability to produce IFNg and TNFa, CD38hi/CD101hi-L14 did not." A bulk population that appears to revert can be reverting entirely in its plastic subfraction. PMID 39196934 transferred BULK sorted NK cells with no equivalent fractionation, so its result is fully compatible with a plastic subset recovering while a fixed subset does not. This converts the row's "SELECTION, NOT PER-CELL REVERSION" from speculation into a documented mechanism in the homologous system. (B) PAUKEN 2016, Science 354:1160, PMID 27789795 — exhaustion-specific chromatin is not remodelled by PD-1 blockade and reinvigoration is transient. A single-timepoint CD107a/IFN-g readout after rest, which is exactly what PMID 39196934 reports, is therefore not sufficient to establish that the underlying state reverted. The Sci Adv study performs no chromatin, methylation or ATAC readout at any point. (C) ABDEL-HAKEEM 2021, Nat Immunol 22:1008, PMID 34312545 (correction 34588688) — "Epigenetic scarring of exhausted T cells hinders memory differentiation upon eliminating chronic antigenic stimulation." This is the transfer-out logic executed properly: remove the chronic signal entirely, and epigenetic scars persist and block normal memory differentiation. Opposite outcome to R2's primary source, in the homologous system, with the chromatin readout R2's primary source lacks. (D) GHONEIM 2017, Cell 170:142, PMID 28648661 — de novo DNA methylation programs restrict PD-1-blockade-mediated rejuvenation; a functional rescue can coexist with an intact restrictive epigenome. (E) TRAINED IMMUNITY / MONOCYTE FIELD — a structural objection that applies to BOTH arms of R2 and that neither the row nor either source addresses. That field's central resolved question is where durable innate epigenetic memory is actually stored, and the answer is not the mature effector: human monocytes live ~5-7 days, far shorter than the years-long persistence of trained phenotypes, and the reservoir is long-lived bone-marrow HSPCs, with BCG-induced transcriptional/epigenetic remodelling demonstrated in the HSPC compartment and conveyed to peripheral CD14+ monocytes months later (Kaufmann 2018 Cell; Cirovic 2020 Cell Host Microbe; reviewed eLife 2025, PMID 40905954). Transplantation of sorted LT-HSCs alone was insufficient, implicating ST-HSC/MPP. Applied to R2: the entire reversible-versus-fixed dispute is being conducted on MATURE NK cells — mature splenic NK transferred for 7-13 days on the reversible side, mature healthy-donor NK in a 96-well plate for 17 days on the fixed side. Neither arm samples the compartment where the innate-memory field found durability to reside, and neither reports a route by which a mature-NK chromatin state would persist through turnover in vivo. That makes the fixed arm's in vitro ATAC signal of unestablished in vivo durability, and simultaneously makes the reversible arm's result less surprising than it is presented to be, since a mature short-lived effector's state is expected to be labile by construction. Whichever way R2 resolves, the experiment that would settle it — an NK progenitor/HSPC-level readout in tumour-bearing animals — has not been run by anyone. claim_text: After TGF-beta withdrawal residency reverts, effector function does not
primary_source_pmid: NO PMID — bioRxiv preprint. Europe PMC ID PPR1223917; DOI 10.64898/2026.02.11.705354; posted 2026-02-14, version 1. bioRxiv API queried 2026-08-14: "no articles found for published version" — NOT peer-reviewed as of audit date.
species: human
what_was_measured: In human peripheral-blood NK cells (healthy adult donors, TUM ethics 2025-584-S-NP), negatively enriched and cultured in vitro in IMDM+ with IL-15 (50 ng/mL) with or without TGF-β (10 ng/mL): cells were exposed to TGF-β for 7 days, then on day 7 either continued on TGF-β to day 17 or washed twice and rested in IL-15 alone for a further 10 days (withdrawal arm), with media exchanged for ALL arms on day 7. At day 17 the readouts were: (a) surface frequencies of CD103+, CD9+, CD49a+ NK cells and intracellular frequencies of GZMA+, GZMB+, IFN-γ+ NK cells by spectral flow cytometry (Cytek Aurora) in n=7 donors across 3 independent experiments; (b) MFI of GZMA and IFN-γ after 3–4 h restimulation with IL-12/IL-18, IL-2+IL-15, IFN-α, or plate-bound anti-NKp46/anti-NKG2D in n=5 donors; (c) bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq on FACS-sorted live CD56+ cells at day 0, day 7 and day 17 in n=5 donors; (d) MitoTracker Green and TMRE at day 17; (e) Ki67. Separately, at 3 h / 24 h / 7 d only (NOT in the day-17 withdrawal arm), impedance-based killing of BxPC-3 PDAC targets at 1:1 E:T by xCELLigence in n=2 / 7 / 10 donors. A sort control separated CD103+ and CD103− NK cells at day 7 and recultured them separately. A separate observational arm profiled tumour-infiltrating NK cells from n=10 liver-tumour patients and blood NK cells from n=12 HCC patients, with ATAC-seq on n=3 HCC vs healthy donors — this arm is cross-sectional and applies no withdrawal.
n_unit: healthy adult human blood donors (day-17 flow phenotype/function, 3 independent experiments); n=5 donors for RNA-seq/ATAC-seq and for restimulation MFI; n=3 donors for CUT&RUN; separate cross-sectional patient cohort n=10 tumour / n=12 blood / n=3 ATAC. NOT cells.
controls: Parallel IL-15-only cultures at every timepoint; media exchange and washing performed for all arms on day 7 so handling is matched; RNA-seq/ATAC-seq analysis explicitly restricted to genes/regions attributable to TGF-β rather than IL-15 at day 7 (Fig. S4A); CD103+ and CD103− cells sorted at day 7 and recultured separately to exclude selective outgrowth of TR-negative cells as the cause of phenotype reversion (Fig. S3A-C); MitoTracker Green/TMRE at day 17 to exclude a metabolic explanation for sustained dysfunction (Fig. S3D); target cells cultured without NK cells as killing-assay control; donor-paired statistics (Wilcoxon signed-rank; paired t-test for Fig. 3E); RIN ≥ 8 gate on RNA; ENCODE blacklist/MAPQ/duplicate filtering on ATAC; yeast spike-in for CUT&RUN. MISSING: no second (longer) withdrawal timepoint beyond 10 days; no TGF-βR inhibitor arm at withdrawal to confirm signal is truly off; no cytotoxicity assay in the day-17 withdrawal arm; no division-tracking dye to match proliferative history between arms; no non-TGF-β dysfunction comparator.
strongest_alternative_explanation: The dissociation may be a difference in RECOVERY TIME CONSTANT, not a difference in reversibility, confounded by differential proliferative history. (1) Only ONE withdrawal duration was tested (10 days), so "effector function does not revert" strictly means "had not yet reverted by day 10." Surface integrins CD103/CD9/CD49a are short-lived, directly SMAD-driven transcripts whose protein turns over fast, so they necessarily decay quickly once signal stops; granule content, IFN-γ competence and chromatin state re-accumulate on intrinsically slower timescales. Two molecule classes with different half-lives sampled at a single post-withdrawal timepoint will always look "dissociated." (2) TGF-β durably suppressed proliferation (reduced Ki67, Fig. S3E). Over the 10-day rest the IL-15-only control is dominated by cells that have divided repeatedly, while the withdrawal arm divides less — so the day-17 comparison confounds cell-intrinsic epigenetic imprinting with differential division history, which is precisely the mechanism by which chromatin marks and protein loads are diluted and reset. No CFSE/CTV division tracking was used to match this. (3) 17 days of continuous high-dose IL-15 in a dish is itself a powerful differentiating and epigenetically remodelling signal; the authors explicitly flag this as unresolved in their limitations. (4) The day-17 "effector function" readout is intracellular granzyme/IFN-γ protein plus transcript and accessibility — a marker proxy. The actual target-cell killing assay was run only at 3 h/24 h/7 d and never in the withdrawal arm, so persistence of the functional deficit itself is not demonstrated by a functional assay. NOTE: the naive alternative — that CD103+ cells were simply outcompeted by CD103− cells — IS excluded by the authors' sort-and-reculture control, which is a genuine strength.
counter_evidence: [audit] FOUND, but indirect — no study located that runs a TGF-β withdrawal design in NK cells and reports the opposite result. (1) Rea A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 40119192 / PMC11957989 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PMC11957989.txt): CRISPR SMAD4 knockout renders human NK cells resistant to TGF-β-mediated loss of NKG2D, granzyme B and cytotoxicity, while CD103/CD49a/ITGB1 induction is MAINTAINED and SMAD4-independent. This corroborates a dissociation between effector suppression and residency induction, but at the PATHWAY level and as PREVENTION (KO before exposure) — it does not test whether an established deficit reverses, so it neither confirms nor refutes R3's temporal claim. (2) Niehrs A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PMC12571907.txt): human liver-transplant cohort shows CD56bright NK cell tissue residency is transient, with TR cells egressing via lymphatics and recirculating — in vivo human support for the "residency phenotype is a labile state" half, and evidentially far stronger than the dish, though it tests no TGF-β withdrawal and measures no effector persistence. (3) Cross-lineage partial counter-evidence, cited by the authors themselves (refs 64-68), that TGF-β-associated lymphocyte dysfunction is at least partly reversible by genetic or pharmacologic interference — e.g. Kwon M et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020, PMID 31941326 (PD-1 blockade plus TGF-β inhibitors reinvigorates myeloma bone-marrow CD8+ T cells) and Tran HC et al., Clin Cancer Res 2017, PMID 27756784 (galunisertib enhances NK-mediated anti-neuroblastoma activity). These involve ACTIVE pathway blockade rather than passive withdrawal, and mostly T cells, so they weaken the generality of "irreversible" without directly refuting the withdrawal experiment. No contradicting NK withdrawal study found. || [adversarial] STRONGEST NEW ITEM — THE PRIOR AUDITOR'S OWN CITATION POINTS THE OTHER WAY. Niehrs A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 (archived refs/R3_PMC12571907.txt) was credited by the prior row as "in vivo human support for the residency-phenotype-is-labile half." Reading the results, it is closer to a counter-observation. Two passages: (1) "NK cells from PB, EXCEPT donor-derived CD56bright NK cells, displayed lower expression of TR markers (CD49a, CXCR6, CD69 and CD103) compared to liver-derived NK cells" — i.e. after human liver transplantation, liver-origin CD56bright NK cells recovered from PERIPHERAL BLOOD, having left the TGF-beta-rich hepatic niche, still carry high CD49a/CXCR6/CD69/CD103. (2) "NK cells within the liver, liver-draining LNs and efferent lymph fluid displayed a consistent phenotype with Aiolos, Eomes, CXCR6 and CD54 expression, indicative of a conserved phenotype throughout the recirculation route" (thoracic-duct cannulation in humans, plus n=2 rhesus macaques). Niehrs shows the CELL's residency is transient (cells egress and are replaced); it does not show the residency PHENOTYPE decays once the cell leaves the niche — it shows the opposite. Those are different propositions and R3's Discussion conflates them (it cites Niehrs ref 70 and infers "TR as a potentially transient state"). Caveats, stated so this is not overread: lymphatic transit is hours-to-days, not 10 days; efferent lymph is not TGF-beta-free; and the explicitly "conserved" markers are Aiolos/Eomes/CXCR6/CD54 rather than CD103/CD49a. Niehrs also contains a genetic control R3 lacks — CRISPR RUNX3 KO in primary human NK cells abolishes TGF-beta-driven CD103 upregulation — showing residency-marker induction is not a bare readout of SMAD occupancy. ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION THE PRIOR AUDITOR MISSED, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THEIRS. "Withdrawal" is never verified to be signal-off, and the paper's own data suggest it may not be. I grepped the full text: pSMAD2/SMAD3 phosphorylation is mentioned only as introductory background and is measured NOWHERE; there is no TGF-betaR inhibitor (SB431542/galunisertib) arm at withdrawal; there is no residual-TGF-beta ELISA. Meanwhile Fig. 4B reports that SMAD3 is among the PERSISTENTLY UPREGULATED genes after withdrawal. NK cells produce TGF-beta autocrinely and 10% FCS carries latent TGF-beta, so a low-level residual signal acting on an upregulated SMAD3 is entirely consistent with the data. Under that model the dissociation is a signal-THRESHOLD effect, not a reversibility difference: CD103/CD9/CD49a induction requires high sustained SMAD input and falls away, while effector repression is maintained by residual low-level signalling. This alternative is cleaner than the prior row's "different protein half-lives" story because it is positively supported by the source's own SMAD3 result, and it is not excluded by any control in the paper. The prior row's proliferation-dilution argument is also mis-signed: reduced Ki67 in the TGF-beta arm means the withdrawal arm divides LESS, which would preserve marks, so dilution cannot explain why residency marks are lost there. CORROBORATING-BUT-NOT-DISPOSITIVE (prior auditor found these; I verified them and sharpen the reading). Rea A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 40119192 / PMC11957989, section header "SMAD4 uncouples TGFbeta inhibition from tissue residency in NK cells": CRISPR SMAD4 KO human NK cells resist TGF-beta-driven loss of effector function while TR integrin/chemokine-receptor induction is preserved SMAD4-independently. This is a peer-reviewed GENETIC dissociation of the two programs in human NK cells — evidentially stronger than R3's washout for the dissociation itself, but it tests prevention, not reversal, so it neither confirms nor refutes R3's temporal claim. Castriconi R et al., PNAS 2003, PMID 12646700 (TGF-beta1 represses NKp30/NKG2D) establishes the acute suppression baseline. Otegbeye F et al., PLoS One 2018, PMID 29342200 (TGF-beta inhibition preserves expanded NK function) is prevention, not rescue of an established deficit. NO DIRECT REFUTATION EXISTS. I ran five distinct searches for an NK study performing TGF-beta washout and reporting functional recovery (queries listed in crossfield_searches_run) and read the returns; none exists. Per G3 this is FOUND-but-indirect, not absence of the phenomenon. R3 is currently the only source running this design in NK cells. downstream_dependency: Directly constrains T1 ("cNK -> trNK, acquisition of a residency phenotype") and T4 ("NK -> ILC1 within tumours"). If CD49a/CD103/CD9 expression is a continuously signal-dependent STATE that decays within 10 days of TGF-β removal, then marker-defined "trNK" and "ILC1-like" endpoints in T1/T4/X3 cannot be read as stable lineage endpoints at all, and any marker-only ancestry inference in those rows is downgraded accordingly. Most concretely, R3's CD103+/CD103− sort-and-reculture control is the exact experimental design that T4's registered Occam alternative ("pre-existing convertible subset is selected") demands, so T4's alternative-explanation analysis can cite it. Load-bearing is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the primary source is a single unrefereed in vitro preprint and because T1/T4 each carry independent in vivo evidence bases (parabiosis, adoptive transfer, transplant genotype) that do not depend on R3.
adversarial_revision: UPHELD. INF_INVITRO UPHELD as strongest class, but on partly different grounds, and the prior row's methods reading contains three verifiable errors. LINEAGE STATUS (batch instruction): R3 is NOT a lineage claim. It asserts nothing of the form "does A give rise to B." It is a two-part functional/state-persistence claim: (i) is a phenotype maintained only while its inducing signal is present, and (ii) does a functional deficit outlast the signal that caused it. No progenitor-product relationship is asserted or tested. Concur with prior auditor on this point only. CLASSIFICATION, re-derived from Methods (refs/R3_PPR1223917.txt, "Cultivation of NK cells", "Bulk RNA sequencing", "Impedance-based killing assay"). Negatively enriched human PB NK cells, 6-12 wells of a 96-well U-bottom plate, IMDM+/10% FCS, rhIL-15 50 ng/mL +/- rhTGF-beta 10 ng/mL. No animal, no transfer, no fate map, no genetic perturbation of any kind (I grepped: no KO, no dominant-negative, no reporter). No OBS_* class applies. Per G2, no pseudotime/velocity/trajectory analysis exists, so INF_TRAJECTORY correctly absent. evidence_types_all [INF_INVITRO, INF_MARKER, INF_KINETIC] upheld. G-RULE CHECK YOU ASKED FOR (population comparison credited as same-cell persistence) — the prior row did not articulate this and it bites at two levels. (a) WITHIN the withdrawal experiment: arms are donor-paired, so not different individuals, but they are different WELLS of cells. There is no barcoding, no division dye, no viability or cell-count reporting per arm, and no single-cell tracking. "The cells that were dysfunctional at day 7 are still dysfunctional at day 17" is a population-frequency inference across separate aliquots — INF_MARKER/INF_KINETIC, never an observation. (b) BETWEEN individuals: Fig. 7D-E compares ATAC-seq of sorted blood NK cells from n=3 HCC patients vs n=3 healthy donors, and Fig. 7C compares n=12 HCC vs healthy controls, to argue chronic TGF-beta imprinting operates in vivo. Cross-sectional, different people, no withdrawal — cannot evidence persistence. The prior auditor noted this arm was cross-sectional but MISSED that Fig. 7D's legend states the patients were selected "with reduced NK-cell functionality (n = 3)" — i.e. the epigenetics comparison is selected on the outcome it is used to explain, and a PCA separating 3 individuals from 3 individuals on the top 80,000 variable features is near-guaranteed regardless of mechanism. THREE ERRORS IN THE PRIOR ROW'S METHODS READING. (1) Wash count is internally contradictory in the source and the prior row reproduced both without noticing: Methods says "transferred to a low-bind tube, washed ONCE with PBS"; Fig. 3A and Fig. 4 legends say "washed TWICE on day 7." The completeness of the central manipulation is not consistently specified. (2) The prior row's controls field asserts "media exchange and washing performed for all arms on day 7 so handling is matched." False. Fig. 3A says media were exchanged for all conditions, but the tube transfer + PBS wash + replating is described ONLY for the withdrawal arm. Handling is NOT matched; the withdrawal arm alone receives an extra mechanical/washing insult before the 10-day rest. (3) Neither the prior row nor the source acknowledges that Methods state "For the 17-day setup, cells were neither handled nor supplemented between days 0-7 and 7-17" — so both arms sat 10 days in unreplenished medium with a single day-7 IL-15 bolus. "No functional recovery" was therefore assayed under progressively depleted culture conditions, and the "continuous TGF-beta" arm is itself a decaying-signal arm. CLAIM-SCOPE ASYMMETRY the prior row understated: the strongest class does not apply uniformly across the two halves. Half (i) (residency reverts) rests on surface staining — INF_MARKER. Half (ii) (effector does not revert) rests ONLY on intracellular GZMA/GZMB/IFN-gamma staining (Fig. 3B-C legends both say "Baseline frequencies", i.e. unstimulated content), restimulation MFI (Fig. 3E, n=5), transcript and accessibility. The xCELLigence killing assay was run at 3 h (n=2), 24 h (n=7) and 7 d (n=10) ONLY — never in any withdrawal arm, at day 17 or at the Fig. 2 6-day-rest arms. The abstract's "sustained suppression of cytotoxicity ... that persists even after signal withdrawal" is therefore not backed by any cytotoxicity measurement. This is exactly the G1 failure mode; the prior auditor flagged it as their "THIRD" overturn and was right to.
crossfield_g4_findings: The mechanism's home field is T cell exhaustion epigenetics, and it supplies both the design standard R3 fails and the specific artefact R3 is most likely showing. 1. DESIGN STANDARD R3 DOES NOT MEET. Philip M et al., Nature 2017, PMID 28514453 / PMC5693219 (archived refs/R3_G4_PMC5693219.txt) states the operational definition directly: "TST dysfunction is initially reversible but ultimately becomes irreversible, EVEN AFTER REMOVAL OF DYSFUNCTIONAL T CELLS FROM THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT AND MULTIPLE ROUNDS OF CELL DIVISION." The field's test for signal-independent epigenetic fixity is (a) remove the cell from the inducing environment in vivo, and (b) demonstrate the state survives division. R3 does neither: no transfer, and no CFSE/CellTrace despite a documented durable Ki67 deficit. Philip also found the same duration threshold R3 reports (plastic state 1 at day 5-7, fixed state 2 from day 14), so R3's structural conclusion is field-consistent and unsurprising — which is a reason to treat it as low-novelty corroboration rather than as load-bearing new evidence. 2. THE SPECIFIC ARTEFACT PHILIP IDENTIFIED, WHICH R3 CANNOT EXCLUDE. Philip sorted CD38lo/CD101lo vs CD38hi/CD101hi cells out of a day-14 population that looked uniformly fixed in bulk; the lo/lo fraction fully regained IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha, the hi/hi fraction did not. A bulk frequency/MFI readout of an apparently "fixed" population can be a MIXTURE of recovered and non-recovered cells. R3's day-17 effector readout is exactly such a bulk readout. Note the asymmetry: R3 ran a sort-and-reculture control (CD103+/CD103-, Fig. S3A-C) for the RESIDENCY half, which is a genuine strength, but ran no heterogeneity control whatsoever for the EFFECTOR half — the half that carries the claim's weight. 3. "DOES NOT SPONTANEOUSLY REVERT" IS NOT "EPIGENETICALLY LOCKED." Ghoneim HE et al., Cell 2017, PMID 28648661: de novo DNMT3A-mediated methylation enforces exhaustion, and DNMT3A deletion or decitabine restores PD-1-blockade rejuvenation. Pauken KE et al., Science 2016, PMID 27789795 and Sen DR et al., Science 2016, PMID 27789799: exhaustion-specific enhancer landscapes are not remodelled by checkpoint blockade and reinvigoration is transient. Abdel-Hakeem MS et al., Nat Immunol 2021, PMID 34312545 (correction 34588688): epigenetic scars persist in vivo after chronic antigen is cleared. Net: durability after passive withdrawal is a real and expected phenomenon, but the causal word in R3's title — "locks" — requires an eraser/writer intervention that R3 never performs. R3 shows correlation between persistent DARs/H3K4me3 loss and persistent dysfunction, not that chromatin is what maintains it. (Searched for the TOX primaries, Khan et al. 2019; my queries returned no hit through lit.py and I did not retrieve them — NOT retrieved, though the TOX literature was not needed to reach this point.) 4. TRAINED IMMUNITY — WHERE THE MEMORY IS ACTUALLY STORED. Kleinnijenhuis J et al., PNAS 2012, PMID 22988082 attributed months-long BCG protection to epigenetic reprogramming of monocytes; because monocytes survive days in circulation, the field relocated the memory to the progenitor compartment: Kaufmann E et al., Cell 2018, PMID 29328912 (BCG educates HSCs); Cirovic B et al., Cell Host Microbe 2020, PMID 32544459 (human BCG trained immunity via the hematopoietic progenitor compartment); Immunity 2024, PMID 39153479 (BCG alters the epigenetic landscape of human bone-marrow progenitors). A closely analogous 2025 result, PMC12571872, shows hypoxia causes H3K4me3 loss in neutrophil PROGENITORS producing long-term functional impairment — the same mark R3 reports lost at effector promoters, but stored one compartment upstream. Bearing on R3: the dish experiment shows a mature human NK cell can hold a dysfunctional state for 10 days, which is a genuine but narrow result. It says nothing about where durable NK dysfunction resides in an HCC patient, and R3's Fig. 7 cross-sectional arm cannot distinguish cell-intrinsic imprinting in mature NK cells from continuous re-imposition on newly produced NK cells or from a reprogrammed progenitor compartment. The trained-immunity field learned this exact lesson the hard way. 5. ADJACENT NK PRECEDENT FOR DURABLE FUNCTIONAL IMPRINTS. Romee R et al., Sci Transl Med 2016, PMID 27655849 and Blood 2012, PMID 22983442: cytokine-induced memory-like NK cells retain an enhanced-function imprint for weeks. Durable functional imprinting in NK cells is established in the positive direction, which raises the prior on R3's phenomenon while doing nothing to validate its measurement.
