adversarial_revision: UPHELD. I re-pulled the primary source myself rather than trusting the row. `lit.py methods 28759001 --tag T4` returns STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T4_28759001.txt); nature.com/articles/ni.3800 via the idp.nature.com redirect chain confirms the narrative Online Methods are paywalled ("Only the abstract and figure thumbnails are accessible"). So the design can only be reconstructed from per-figure legend pages, as the auditor said. On that basis: STRONGEST CLASS = OBS_TRANSFER: UPHELD. Fig 4d legend, verbatim from the publisher figure page: "CD45.1+ mice were given subcutaneous transplantation of MCA1956 cells on day 0, followed by intratumoral (i.t.) injection of CD45.2+ splenic NK cells on day 14 and analysis on days 18 and 21." That is literally "transfer A, recover B in recipient" in an immunocompetent congenic host. It is NOT marker similarity alone, NOT in vitro, NOT pseudotime. No OBS_DIRECT exists (no barcoding, no clonal tracking, no inducible fate map), so OBS_TRANSFER is correctly the ceiling. OBS_GENETIC is defensible for Fig 4h-j (Tgfbr2-deleted DONOR NK cells fail to yield the output; n=7 RII-WT vs n=5 RII-FL, P<0.05) though it is a within-transfer modifier, not an independent genetic lineage test, and it is a partial reduction rather than an absence. BUT THREE MATERIAL ERRORS IN THE ROW, one of which narrows the claim: (1) THE ROW MISSTATES WHAT THE CLEAN ARM MEASURED. The row's what_was_measured says Fig 4d-g scored "donor-derived CD49a+CD49b+Eomes+ 'intILC1' AND CD49a+CD49b-Eomes-int 'ILC1' events." The legend says otherwise. Verbatim: "(e) Flow cytometry of host (CD45.1+) and donor (CD45.2+) tumor group 1 ILC subsets (above plots) from host mice as in d at day 18 or 21. (f) Quantification of NK cell-derived intILC1s as in e." Only intILC1 is quantified. Donor-derived bona fide ILC1 (CD49a+CD49b-Eomes-int) is NOT reported in the intratumoural immunocompetent arm. Consequence: the ONE arm free of the lymphopenia confound establishes, at OBS_TRANSFER grade, only NK -> intILC1 — an intermediate that still expresses CD49b and Eomes, i.e. still NK-like. Donor-derived terminal ILC1 in a tumour is reported only in the Rag2-/-gc-/- arm (Fig 4a-c, i.v., day 3 -> day 18, n=6), which is exactly the arm confounded by lymphopenia-driven CD49a upregulation. So the claim as literally stated — "NK -> ILC1 inside tumours" — has its clean OBS_TRANSFER support only for the intermediate state, and its ILC1 endpoint only in an empty-niche host. (2) THE ROW'S PROVENANCE CLAIM FOR CORTEZ IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. It states "Cortez 2017 methods WERE fully obtained via PMC5712491." The archived file /home/user/aaa/refs/T4_PMC5712491.txt carries the header "# status=ABSTRACT_ONLY pmid=28759002 pmcid=PMC5712491" — it is abstract + reference list only. I independently re-fetched pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5712491 and the row's SUBSTANTIVE conclusions do hold: no adoptive transfer anywhere in Cortez; Ncr1-iCre and Il7r-Cre appear only as conditional-deletion drivers with no Rosa26 reporter, so no fate map; B16-F10 readout is "1 x 10^5 B16-F10 ... injected into the tail vein ... At day 15 ... tumor foci were quantified in the lungs." n is weak: "one to three mice per genotype," microarray "n = 3 biological replicates." So the conclusion survives but the stated provenance does not. (3) THE ROW'S CENTRAL NEGATIVE SEARCH CLAIM IS FALSE — see new_counter_evidence. It asserts "Searched specifically for true fate mapping of the NK-to-ILC1 axis and found none, in tumours or otherwise." Such a study exists and is directly contradictory.
crossfield_g4_findings: The row ran ZERO cross-field searches — every one of its 24 listed searches is inside the NK/ILC1 tumour field. Rule G4 is unmet in the row. I searched the TRM, ILC and myeloid literature on the same process (circulating cell -> tissue-resident cell; TGF-beta-driven residency programming). Those fields have already adjudicated exactly this question, and they adjudicated it AGAINST the bulk-transfer design Gao used. (1) T CELL / TRM FIELD — THE DECISIVE METHODOLOGICAL RESULT. Kok L, Dijkgraaf FE, Urbanus J, Bresser K, ... Perie L, Beltman JB, Schumacher TN. "A committed tissue-resident memory T cell precursor within the circulating CD8+ effector T cell pool." J Exp Med 2020;217(10):e20191711. PMID 32728699, PMC7537386 (OA full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T4_PMC7537386.txt). Design: a ~200,000-member retroviral barcode library (BC2.0), thymocytes transduced and injected intrathymically so naive T cells are labelled WITHOUT in vitro activation; 500-1,000 barcoded naive OT-I cells transferred per recipient; skin DNA vaccination; barcode sequencing of TEFF (d12), TRM and TCIRCM (d>60); plus scRNA-seq with barcodes in the GFP 3'UTR, recovering clonal identity for 1,527 of 5,383 cells across 151 clones. Findings that bear directly on T4: (a) The field's canonical answer is SELECTION OF A PRE-COMMITTED SUBSET, not conversion. Verbatim: "these data reveal that, before skin entry, the ability of TEFF to form TRM is differentially and permanently imprinted at a clonal level," and "definitive evidence for the existence of a circulating TRM precursor population that commits to the TRM-fate before tissue entrance." ~29.7% of clones were TRM-biased, 16.9% TCIRCM-biased, and this was independent of clonal burst size. (b) THE CONTROL THAT SETTLES IT — one Gao never ran. Vaccinating LEFT and RIGHT hind-leg skin in the same mouse: if the tissue instructs conversion, the two sites should be clonally disparate; if a pre-committed precursor is selected, they should match. Result: r = 0.78 between the two anatomically separate TRM pools versus r = 0.30-0.37 between skin TRM and circulating memory. Two independent, spatially separated "tissues" drawing from the same donor pool is the cheap, decisive discriminator between selection and conversion. Gao's design has no such internal replicate — a single tumour per mouse, n=3-4 mice. (c) They also excluded stochastic engraftment explicitly by in-silico simulation of founder pools of three sizes, and showed it "could not explain the observed skewing." Gao offers no analogous test. (d) MOST DAMAGING SPECIFIC POINT: the markers Gao uses to define the converted state are, in the home field, markers of the PRE-EXISTING CIRCULATING PRECURSOR. Kok's blood-borne "TRM-like MP" effector state, present in the CIRCULATION at day 12, is "strongly enriched for core TRM signature genes, such as Itgae (CD103), ITGA1 (CD49A), and Fabp5," and shows "moderate to high expression of the IL-15 (Il2rb) and TGFbeta (Tgfbr1) receptors." CD49a/Itga1 is therefore demonstrably expressed by a minority pre-committed subset BEFORE tissue entry. Recovering CD49a+ donor cells after transfer is exactly what selection of a CD49a-poised minority predicts, and Gao's live sort gate could not have excluded it (Eomes is intracellular and requires fixation, so the "CD49a-CD49b+Eomes+" input was defined post hoc; no purity figure is reported in any legend). This converts the row's alternative from a reasonable worry into the home field's established default. (2) TRM FIELD, ASSAY LESSON. Anderson KG, Mayer-Barber K, Sung H, ... Masopust D. "Intravascular staining for discrimination of vascular and tissue leukocytes." Nat Protoc 2014;9:209-222, PMID 24385150. The lesson: flow cytometry of enzymatically disaggregated non-lymphoid tissue systematically misassigns blood-borne and vessel-adherent lymphocytes as tissue-resident unless an intravascular label is given minutes before sacrifice. This became mandatory in TRM work after 2014. Gao's tumour digests report no intravascular labelling; donor cells scored as "in the tumour" are not separated from donor cells in tumour vasculature. Notably, Gasteiger 2015 (the ILC parabiosis paper) does cite Anderson 2014 — the ILC field adopted the control; the Gao tumour arm did not. (3) ILC FIELD, RESIDENCY vs ORIGIN. Gasteiger et al. Science 2015 (PMID 26472762) used PARABIOSIS to show ILCs are "maintained by self-renewal in broadly different microenvironments" and only "at later time points after infection" do "cells from hematogenous sources help to partially replenish the pool." Parabiosis answers the question Gao's transfer cannot: what is the source of the resident pool in an UNMANIPULATED animal. The methodological lesson the TRM field learned the hard way and states plainly — parabiosis and chimerism establish RESIDENCY and REPLENISHMENT RATE, not the identity of the precursor; and conversely, an adoptive transfer establishes CAPACITY, not the physiological route. Gao demonstrates capacity. No parabiosis, no photoconversion (cf. Kaede), and no inducible fate map was done for the tumour ILC1 pool. (4) MYELOID FIELD — THE EMPTY-NICHE ARTEFACT, WHICH IS WHAT GAO'S Rag2-/-gc-/- ARMS ACTUALLY MEASURE. van de Laar L, Saelens W, De Prijck S, ... Lambrecht BN, Guilliams M. "Yolk Sac Macrophages, Fetal Liver, and Adult Monocytes Can Colonize an Empty Niche and Develop into Functional Tissue-Resident Macrophages." Immunity 2016;44:755-768, PMID 26992565. Verbatim: three developmentally unrelated precursors were transferred "into the empty alveolar macrophage (AM) niche of neonatal Csf2rb(-/-) mice"; "when transferred separately, however, ALL precursors efficiently colonized the alveolar niche and generated AMs that were transcriptionally ALMOST IDENTICAL, self-maintained, and durably prevented alveolar proteinosis"; conclusion: "precursor origin does not affect the development of functional self-maintaining tissue-resident macrophages." Direct read-across: Gao's Fig 3e and Fig 4a-c transfer NK cells into Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts, which have a COMPLETELY EMPTY group-1-ILC niche. Recovering "ILC1-phenotype" donor cells there demonstrates that the niche can impose the resident phenotype on a competent precursor — the myeloid field's textbook result — and says nothing about whether NK cells are the physiological source in an intact tumour-bearing animal. Note also van de Laar's competition result: when precursors were co-transferred, one subset preferentially outgrew the others "correlating with their superior ... proliferation capacity." That is the row's selective-outgrowth alternative, demonstrated experimentally, and it maps onto Gao's own Fig 3e (intILC1s carry the highest Ki67 among group 1 ILC subsets, n=3 host mice at d7 and n=4 at d14). (5) MYELOID FIELD, HISTORICAL PRECEDENT FOR THIS EXACT ERROR. The pre-2010 consensus that blood monocytes convert into microglia and other tissue-resident macrophages rested on bulk transfer plus irradiation-chimera data, and was overturned only when inducible genetic fate mapping was applied (Ginhoux 2010 Science; Yona 2013 and Hashimoto 2013 Immunity; reviewed by Guilliams & Scott). The failure mode was precisely Gao's: a perturbed/emptied host plus a marker-defined readout was read as ontogeny. NOT_SEARCHED disclosure: I did not re-pull those four myeloid fate-mapping methods sections individually; I searched and read van de Laar 2016 (PMID 26992565, verified via lit.py fetch) and rely on the others as field context rather than as audited primary evidence. SYNTHESIS. All three home fields converge on the same verdict about Gao's assay: bulk congenic transfer of a marker-sorted population into a tumour, read out by the same markers, is a CAPACITY assay. In the T-cell field the equivalent conclusion was overturned by clonal barcoding, which showed pre-commitment before tissue entry — and showed that CD49a itself marks the pre-committed circulating minority. In the myeloid field the equivalent conclusion was overturned by inducible fate mapping, and empty-niche transfer was shown to homogenise phenotype irrespective of origin. In the ILC field parabiosis showed the resident pool self-renews locally. The one field that has now applied the correct tool to this exact axis — Nixon 2022's Gzmc and S1pr5 knock-in fate maps — found NO NK-to-ILC1 interconversion and an ILC-progenitor origin.

species: Human (Homo sapiens) only. Peripheral blood from female Hong Kong Red Cross blood donors; first-trimester decidua and placenta from women undergoing surgical termination of pregnancy; HUVEC. No animal work anywhere in the paper.
what_was_measured: In human cells in vitro: peripheral-blood CD16-CD56bright NK cells were negatively immuno-magnetically separated and CD56-microbead-enriched from female Hong Kong Red Cross blood donations (purity >95%), then 1x10^6 cells were cultured 5 days in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS + 500 IU/mL rhIL-2 + 5 ng/mL rhIL-15, with or without 5 ug/mL glycodelin-A immuno-affinity-purified from human amniotic fluid. At day 5 the readouts were: surface CD9, CD49a, CD151, CD158a and intracellular VEGF by flow cytometry (N=5 donors); secreted angiogenic proteins by cytokine array and VEGF/IGFBP-1 by ELISA (N=3); GdA binding and surface L-selectin/Siglec-7 by flow cytometry on normal vs sialidase-treated GdA (N=4); GdA/L-selectin association by immunoprecipitation; ERK phosphorylation by Western blot; and functional assays on GdA-conditioned NK spent media — HUVEC tube formation and trans-well migration, and trans-well invasion/migration of primary first-trimester extravillous trophoblasts — with anti-VEGF/anti-IGFBP-1 and anti-L-selectin blocking antibodies. Only CD9, CD49a and VEGF rose significantly (P<0.05); CD151 and CD158a did not shift to the dNK pattern. The measurement is day-5 marker and secretome drift in a bulk, cytokine-driven culture — no cell was observed to become another cell.
n: 5 (main flow-cytometry marker experiments); 4 (GdA-binding / L-selectin / Siglec-7 experiments); 3 (angiogenesis cytokine array). Number of decidual-tissue donors and first-trimester placental donors: NOT STATED in the retrievable text.
n_unit: independent human peripheral-blood donors (Hong Kong Red Cross blood donations), NOT cells. Cells per condition were 1x10^6, which is an input quantity, not a replicate count.
controls: (1) Vehicle-equivalent control: "NK cells cultured under the same conditions without GdA were used as the control" — i.e. the control arm still received 500 IU/mL IL-2 + 5 ng/mL IL-15 for 5 days, so the comparison is GdA-on-top-of-strong-cytokine-stimulation, not GdA vs quiescence. (2) Isotype IgG for flow cytometry. (3) De-sialylated GdA (sialidase-agarose treated) as a glycan-dependence control. (4) Anti-L-selectin functional blocking antibody; anti-VEGF and anti-IGFBP-1 blocking antibodies in the HUVEC/trophoblast assays. (5) CD16+CD56dim NK cells as a comparator subset for binding. (6) Primary dNK cells shown alongside treated blood NK in some figures as a phenotypic reference. NOT present: any protein/glycoprotein-load control (e.g. BSA or an irrelevant sialylated glycoprotein at 5 ug/mL), heat-denatured GdA, a cell-number/proliferation readout, CFSE dilution, or a day-0 baseline frequency of CD9+/CD49a+ cells within the CD56bright gate. Viability was addressed only as "GdA treatment at the concentration used did not affect the viability of NK cells as demonstrated by XTT viability assay (data not shown)."
strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION/EXPANSION OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET, which this design cannot exclude. Peripheral-blood CD56bright NK cells are not uniform for CD9 or CD49a; GdA binds via sialylated glycans to L-selectin, which the paper itself shows is expressed on CD56bright but not CD56dim cells, and L-selectin ligation plus 5 days of 500 IU/mL IL-2 and IL-15 is a potent survival/proliferation signal. A GdA-driven survival or proliferative advantage for the CD9+CD49a+ fraction already present at day 0 would produce exactly the observed bulk shift with no cell ever changing identity. Nothing in the methods discriminates the two: no CFSE/CTV dilution, no barcoding, no clonal or single-cell tracking, no absolute cell counts, no day-0 subset frequency, and viability only as unshown XTT data. A second, independent alternative is MARKER ARTEFACT OF PROLIFERATION: CD9 is acquired by ordinary NK cells during cytokine-driven cell-cycle entry — Orrantia et al. (iScience 2022, PMID 36262311) found blood NK cells acquire a "decidual-like" transcriptional profile including CD9 during post-autoHSCT reconstitution dominated by cell-cycle and DNA-replication programmes, and those CD9+ cells carried HIGHER granzyme B and perforin, the opposite of the tolerogenic dNK phenotype. A third: the phenotype is not GdA-specific — hypoxia + TGF-beta1 + 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine (Cerdeira et al., J Immunol 2013, PMID 23487420) and TGF-beta alone (Keskin et al., PNAS 2007, PMID 17360654) already produce CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ "dNK-like" cells, so a 2-of-4-marker shift is a generic culture output rather than evidence of a GdA-instructed lineage decision. The paper's own data undercut conversion: CD151 and CD158a, the other two dNK markers assayed, did NOT convert.
counter_evidence: [audit] FOUND — searched and read. (1) Orrantia et al., iScience 2022;25:105235 (PMID 36262311 / PMC9574507, full text archived): CD9+ "decidual-like" NK cells expand IN VIVO in human blood after autologous HSCT during a proliferation-dominated reconstitution and express MORE granzyme B and perforin than CD9- NK cells — decoupling CD9/decidual-like gene signature from the non-cytotoxic dNK identity and showing the marker tracks proliferation, not decidualization. (2) Niehrs et al., Nat Immunol 2025 (PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907, archived): human CD56bright NK cells show TRANSIENT tissue residency with lymphatic egress and recirculation, so acquisition of residency-associated markers by CD56bright cells is reversible traffic biology, not a terminal lineage conversion. (3) Vacca et al., PNAS 2011;108:2402-7 (PMID 21248224): CD34+ haematopoietic precursors resident in human decidua differentiate into NK cells on contact with decidual stromal cells — an origin for dNK that requires no blood-NK conversion at all. (4) Sojka et al., eLife 2014 (PMC3975579): tissue-resident uterine NK/ILC1 are a lineage distinct from conventional circulating NK cells — the two-independent-origins alternative. (5) Priority/specificity counter-evidence: Keskin 2007 (PNAS, TGF-beta) and Cerdeira 2013 (J Immunol, hypoxia+TGF-beta1+decitabine) obtained the same CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ readout from unrelated stimuli. NOT FOUND despite searching: any direct replication of the GdA-specific result by an independent laboratory, and any experiment (of any kind) testing GdA-driven dNK conversion in vivo. || [adversarial] THREE items the auditor missed, one of which is decisive, plus an internal contradiction in the auditor's own list. (1) DECISIVE MISS — Dixit A & Karande AA, "Glycodelin regulates the numbers and function of peripheral natural killer cells," J Reprod Immunol 2020;137:102625, PMID 31730930 (Indian Institute of Science; archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_31730930.txt). This is the ONLY independent-laboratory primary study of glycodelin acting on human peripheral NK cells, published within a year of Lee 2019, and it is not in the auditor's row at all. It reports that glycodelin "suppresses the cytotoxicity of peripheral NK cells via downregulating perforin, granzyme B and IFNgamma" and — the load-bearing sentence — "Glycodelin also induces caspase-dependent death in ONLY ACTIVATED peripheral NK cells," mediated by CD7, not L-selectin. Selective killing of the activated, cytotoxic, perforin/granzyme-high fraction is a concrete, published, independently-observed MECHANISM that would generate Lee 2019's exact bulk marker shift with no cell ever changing identity: kill the cytotoxic CD9-negative cells and the surviving mean drifts toward CD9+CD49a+VEGF+. This converts the "pre-existing subset was selected, not converted" alternative from a generic design criticism into a specific mechanism demonstrated for this very ligand on this very cell type — and Lee 2019's only rebuttal is an XTT assay shown as "data not shown". It also creates a receptor conflict (Karande: CD7; Lee: L-selectin) for the same ligand on the same cell. The Karande group had already reported GdA-induced NK apoptosis in PMID 29271477 (2018), i.e. BEFORE Lee 2019. (2) MAJOR MISS on marker specificity AND on pre-existence — Gallazzi M, ..., Albini A, Noonan DM, Bruno A, "Prostate Cancer Peripheral Blood NK Cells Show Enhanced CD9, CD49a, CXCR4, CXCL8, MMP-9 Production...," Front Immunol 2020;11:586126, PMID 33569050 / PMC7868409 (OA full text archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_PMC7868409.txt), with its predecessor Bruno et al., FASEB J 2018, PMID 29763380 ("proangiogenic, decidual NK-like cells from patients with colorectal cancer" — note: PRE-dates Lee 2019). Verbatim from the full text: "PCa pTA-NKs acquire the CD56bright CD9+ CD49a+ CXCR4+ phenotype", measured DIRECTLY EX VIVO by flow cytometry on PBMC from prostate cancer patients — men, no pregnancy, no decidua, no glycodelin, no culture — with elevated VEGF mRNA. This establishes that CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ "dNK-like" NK cells PRE-EXIST in human peripheral blood and vary in frequency with host state, which is exactly the pre-existing pool the selection alternative requires and which Lee 2019 never quantifies at day 0. The same paper then shows the readout is stimulus-nonspecific three ways over: TGF-beta at 10 ng/mL for 72 h raised CD56 (p<=0.01), CD9 (p<=0.01) and CD49a (p<=0.05) on healthy-donor blood NK; conditioned media from three unrelated prostate cancer lines (PC-3, DU-145, LNCaP) for 72 h likewise raised CD9, CD49a and CXCR4; and IL-6 did not. So four mechanistically unrelated inputs (GdA, TGF-beta, tumour secretome, and per Cerdeira 2013 hypoxia+TGF-beta1+decitabine) converge on the same 2-marker readout. This is a generic pro-angiogenic/exhausted NK polarization state, not a GdA-instructed decidual lineage decision. The auditor cited Orrantia 2022, Keskin 2007 and Cerdeira 2013 for a weaker version of this point and missed the cancer-blood literature entirely. (3) MISS that cuts BOTH ways, and exposes an internal contradiction in the auditor's row — Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, "Tissue-resident natural killer cells derived from conventional natural killer cells are regulated by progesterone in the uterus," Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390-401, PMID 39708955 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_39708955.txt). Mouse, IN VIVO, parabiosis + intravascular fluorescent antibody labeling + ovariectomy + hormone add-back + progesterone-receptor antagonist: "Our parabiosis studies confirmed that the progesterone-responsive trNK cells are derived from peripheral cNK cells," and "mice OVX at three weeks of age and analyzed as adults lacked uterine trNK cells unless progesterone was administered." Three consequences. (a) It REHABILITATES the general premise the auditor tried to attack — blood cNK really can give rise to uterine tissue-resident NK — so the auditor's blanket "two independent origins" framing is too strong. (b) It supplies a COMPETING, far better-evidenced sufficient driver: progesterone, tested by parabiosis and by receptor antagonist, in vivo. GdA is not needed to explain uterine NK residency. (c) Critically, it is by DOROTHY SOJKA, the senior author of the very eLife 2014 paper (PMID 24714492) the auditor cited as counter-evidence #4 for "two independent origins". crossfield_g4_findings: The mechanism T5 invokes is generic: a circulating lymphocyte acquires a tissue-residency/tolerogenic program under a locally secreted factor. The TRM, ILC and myeloid fields have each already run this exact question with assays Lee 2019 does not use, and all three converge on the same verdict: a bulk marker shift in culture is not evidence of conversion, and every time the question was settled properly the answer changed. (A) TRM — WHAT THE FIELD REQUIRED AS PROOF. Mackay LK et al., Nat Immunol 2013, PMID 24162776, "The developmental pathway for CD103+CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells of skin": the field did NOT accept TGF-beta-induced CD103 in a dish as demonstrating that circulating cells become resident. It required transfer of congenically/TCR-marked cells into recipients with in vivo tracking of the SAME marked cells — an OBS_TRANSFER design. Zhang N & Bevan MJ, Immunity 2013, PMID 24076049, "Transforming growth factor-beta signaling controls the formation and maintenance of gut-resident memory T cells by regulating migration and retention": conditional deletion of the TGF-beta receptor in T cells so that TRM fail to form — an OBS_GENETIC design. That is the evidentiary bar for "factor X converts A into tissue-resident B", and note that both papers concern TGF-beta, the very cytokine that Gallazzi 2020 (PMID 33569050) shows reproduces GdA's entire CD9/CD49a readout. The TRM field cleared this bar in 2013; T5 has not cleared it in 2026. (B) TRM — THE MARKER ITSELF IS AN ACTIVATION MARKER. Shiow LR et al., Nature 2006, PMID 16525420, "CD69 acts downstream of interferon-alpha/beta to inhibit S1P1 and lymphocyte egress from lymphoid organs": the canonical residency marker CD69 is an activation-induced protein, so any activating culture manufactures "residency" phenotype by construction. This is the single most transferable lesson to T5. Lee 2019 cultured for 5 days in 500 IU/mL IL-2 plus 5 ng/mL IL-15 — a maximally activating condition — and scored CD49a (ITGA1, an activation-inducible adhesion integrin) and CD9 (a tetraspanin induced on cycling/activated lymphocytes). Because the GdA arm and the control arm both received the cytokines, the paper controls for the cytokines' MEAN effect but not for a GdA x activation interaction, and not at all for differential survival across the pre-existing activation states within the gate — which is exactly what Karande's PMID 31730930 says GdA does (kills ONLY activated NK cells). (C) TRM — THE FIELD HAD TO INVENT A CONTROL TO SEPARATE "IS IN THE TISSUE" FROM "IS OF THE TISSUE". Anderson KG et al., Nat Protoc 2014, PMID 24385150, intravascular staining: a large fraction of lymphocytes recovered by tissue digestion and called resident were in fact still vascular. Structural analogue for T5: the field learned that you cannot infer a cell's identity from the compartment-level readout without a control that separates the two populations. Lee 2019 has no control separating "a CD56bright cell became CD9+CD49a+" from "a CD9+CD49a+ CD56bright cell was already there and outlived its neighbours." (D) ILC — PARABIOSIS IS THE ARBITER, AND IT HAS ALREADY BEEN RUN ON THIS EXACT TISSUE. Gasteiger G, Fan X, Dikiy S, Lee SY, Rudensky AY, Science 2015, PMID 26472762, "Tissue residency of innate lymphoid cells in lymphoid and nonlymphoid organs": parabiosis established that ILCs in nonlymphoid organs are largely tissue-resident and are NOT replenished from the circulation at steady state, placing the burden of proof on anyone claiming blood-to-tissue conversion. Then Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025, PMID 39708955, ran parabiosis plus intravascular labeling plus ovariectomy plus PR antagonist on the UTERUS specifically and found uterine trNK ARE cNK-derived and progesterone-driven. So for the precise biological question behind T5, an OBS_DIRECT-grade in vivo answer already exists in mouse — and it names progesterone, not glycodelin, as the driver. Glycodelin cannot be tested this way at all (PAEP is primate-restricted; PMID 29271477). The correct reading is therefore not "conversion is impossible" but "conversion is real, has been demonstrated by parabiosis with a different and better-evidenced driver, and GdA's specific contribution remains untested by any assay capable of detecting it." (E) MYELOID — THE CANONICAL CAUTIONARY TALE, AND IT IS AN EXACT STRUCTURAL MATCH. "Blood monocytes convert into tissue macrophages" was textbook for decades on the strength of marker similarity and in vitro differentiation — the same two evidence classes as T5. It was overturned by fate mapping: Ginhoux F et al., Science 2010, PMID 20966214, showed adult microglia derive from yolk-sac primitive macrophages, not blood monocytes; Hashimoto D et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23601688, showed by parabiosis and fate mapping that tissue-resident macrophages self-maintain locally with minimal monocyte input. The specific error in the old literature was reading a bulk phenotype shift as conversion when the real driver was LOCAL PROLIFERATION of a pre-existing resident population — numerically identical to the confound in T5, and the reason CFSE/CTV, absolute counts and day-0 frequencies are non-optional. (F) MYELOID — CULTURE IS THE WRONG PLACE TO DEMONSTRATE ACQUISITION OF A TISSUE IDENTITY. Lavin Y et al., Cell 2014, PMID 25480296, and Gosselin D et al., Cell 2014, PMID 25480297, showed the tissue environment writes the macrophage enhancer landscape and that removing macrophages from tissue into culture rapidly erases the tissue-specific program. If a genuine tissue identity is continuously imposed by the environment and is lost within days ex vivo, then a 5-day dish containing one purified protein is close to the least capable system for demonstrating that a cell has ACQUIRED that identity — the assay is running against the biology. This is a general methodological verdict from an adjacent field that applies directly and was not considered in the row under review. NET G4 VERDICT: the cross-field literature does not overturn the possibility of blood-NK-to-uterine-NK conversion — Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 supports it — but it comprehensively overturns the SUFFICIENCY of Lee 2019's evidence for it, identifies the precise uncontrolled confounds (activation-induced markers, proliferation, differential survival), names the assays that would settle it (congenic/adoptive transfer, parabiosis, barcoding, CFSE, conditional receptor deletion), and supplies a better-evidenced competing driver (progesterone).
primary_source_citation: Lee CL, Vijayan M, Wang X, Lam KKW, Koistinen H, Seppälä M, Li RHW, Ng EHY, Yeung WSB, Chiu PCN. "Glycodelin-A stimulates the conversion of human peripheral blood CD16-CD56bright NK cell to a decidual NK cell-like phenotype." Hum Reprod. 2019 Apr 1;34(4):689-701. doi:10.1093/humrep/dey378. PMID 30597092. This is the FIRST and, as of this audit, the ONLY primary paper asserting GdA-driven dNK conversion. Prior GdA/NK primary work from the same Hong Kong group (Lee CL et al., Fertil Steril 2010;94:769-71, PMID 19945098) reported only cytokine modulation (IL-6, IL-13, GM-CSF) with explicitly no effect on viability or cytotoxicity, and made no conversion claim; Bolton et al., Am J Reprod Immunol 1991 (PMID 1840727, PP14/glycodelin suppresses NK activity) is a function-suppression claim, not a lineage claim. So priority for "GdA converts NK toward dNK" rests entirely on Lee 2019.

species: Human (Homo sapiens). Peripheral blood from anonymous healthy French volunteer donors, Etablissement Français du Sang Lyon, convention 16-093. No animals used anywhere in the paper.
what_was_measured: In human PBMC-derived NK cells (negatively selected, purity >90%; or FACS-sorted CD56+CD3-NKG2C+ vs NKG2C-, purity >98%), cultured in vitro in RPMI + 20% human AB serum + IL-2 (100 IU/mL) with or without recombinant IL-35 (PeproTech 200-37, 100 ng/mL, medium renewed every 2 days), at days 2, 4 and 8, surface expression of CD9, CD103 (ITGAE) and CD49a (ITGA1) was measured by spectral flow cytometry (Cytek Aurora / LSRFortessa) alongside intracellular EOMES, T-BET and IFN-γ, in 3 individual donors (Fig 5a, 5d), 5 donors (Fig 5f) and 3-6 donors (Fig 6f, TGF-β blockade); in parallel, 10x Genomics 3' v3.1 scRNA-seq with CellPlex CMO condition-hashing was run at days 2 and 4 on 2 donors (~5,000 cells per condition) and an "ILC1-like" UCell gene-signature score was computed per cell. Readout is the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events per well, compared paired within donor against the IL-2-alone arm — not any per-cell or per-clone tracking of a given NK cell acquiring the phenotype.
n: 3 donors for the core CD9/CD103/CD49a conversion kinetics (Fig 5a, 5d); 5 donors (Fig 5f); 3-6 donors for the TGF-β-blockade rescue (Fig 6f); 2 donors for scRNA-seq. Largest n supporting the marker claim = 5.
n_unit: healthy human blood donors (biological replicates); NOT cells. The 354,379-cell / 108-patient-sample figures elsewhere in the paper are in-silico re-analysis of four public tumour scRNA-seq datasets (GSE131907, GSE160269, GSE166555, GSE176078), not experimental n for this claim.
controls: Paired same-donor IL-2-alone arm (paired t-test) for every conversion timepoint. Viability/survival control: NK survival statistically identical ±IL-35 out to day 9, so reduced cell number is not selective death. CTV proliferation assay: IL-35 significantly REDUCES proliferation. Purity controls: bulk NK >90%, FACS-sorted NKG2C+ and NKG2C- each >98%, and both sorted subsets converted. Mechanistic controls: anti-TGF-β1/2/3 (R&D MAB1835) vs mouse IgG1 isotype (MAB002), and Galunisertib (TGF-βR inhibitor) vs DMSO vehicle, both of which prevented acquisition of CD9/CD103/CD49a. TGF-β alone (1 ng/mL) used as positive control for conversion. IL-35 washout/starvation arm (3 washes + 48 h) to test reversibility. MISSING control: the starting population was never sorted or gated to be CD9-CD103-CD49a-, so a pre-existing tissue-residency-marker-positive fraction is not formally excluded at t=0; and the bulk >90% purity leaves up to ~10% non-NK contaminants in the non-sorted experiments.
strongest_alternative_explanation: Selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing CD9+CD103+CD49a+ subset, plus a culture artefact of supraphysiological cytokine exposure. The paper argues against pure selection reasonably well but not decisively: IL-35 SUPPRESSES proliferation and does not alter survival, so neither preferential expansion nor preferential death of the CD49a- majority is an easy explanation, and "nearly all cells" are marker-positive by day 8, which is arithmetically hard to reach by selecting a near-absent blood precursor without proliferation; both >98%-pure NKG2C+ and NKG2C- sorted subsets converted, so it is not one contaminating subset. What remains genuinely unexcluded: (1) no clonal or per-cell tracking exists — the CellPlex CMO barcoding is SAMPLE/CONDITION hashing, not lineage barcoding, so no individual NK cell was ever observed to acquire the phenotype; the entire claim rests on population-frequency shifts between wells; (2) t=0 was never sorted CD9-CD103-CD49a-; (3) the phenotype is defined by three integrins/tetraspanin plus a signature score, and TGF-β is long known to induce exactly these markers on cultured blood NK cells, so "ILC1-like conversion" may be a reversible TGF-β-driven phenotypic state rather than a lineage change (EOMES fell but T-BET was unchanged — an incomplete ILC1 transcription-factor switch); (4) reagent artefact — see counter_evidence.
counter_evidence: [audit] FOUND, three strands. (1) REAGENT VALIDITY: Aparicio-Siegmund et al., PLoS One 2014;9(9):e107990, PMID 25259790, "Recombinant p35 from Bacteria Can Form Interleukin (IL-)12, but Not IL-35" — reconstituted recombinant IL-35 failed to induce STAT1/STAT3 phosphorylation and failed to induce proliferation of Ba/F3-gp130-IL-12Rβ1-IL-12Rβ2 cells; the authors "fail to create IL-35 by this approach". Partial mitigation: PeproTech 200-37 as used here is a HEK293-expressed 406-aa single-chain IL-12A-EBI3 fusion (~45.8 kDa), not a bacterial reconstitution — but it is still a non-native single-chain construct used at 100 ng/mL, a high dose, and the field-wide reagent caveat is unresolved. (2) MECHANISTIC DISPLACEMENT — the strongest counter to the claim AS WORDED: the paper's own data show conversion is mediated by AUTOCRINE TGF-β, is completely abrogated by anti-TGF-β1/2/3 or Galunisertib, and is reproduced by TGF-β alone. The pre-existing primary literature already established TGF-β-driven NK→CD49a+CD103+CD9+ ILC1-like conversion (Gao et al., Nat Immunol 2017, PMID 28759001, mouse, with genetic fate mapping; Cortez et al. 2016, PMID 27156386). So IL-35 is an upstream inducer of TGF-β, not the differentiation signal itself; "IL-35 drives NK toward an ILC1-like phenotype" is one causal step removed from what was measured. (3) NO INDEPENDENT REPLICATION of the conversion: the only independent IL-35/NK primary paper found (PMID 41357575, 2025, IL-35 suppression of NK immunosurveillance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC) corroborates only the suppression half and does not test CD9/CD103/CD49a or ILC1-like conversion. Separately, a targeted search for a paper directly refuting in vitro NK→ILC1-like conversion as a marker artefact was run and returned zero hits — searched and not found, not "does not exist". Also noted: the paper's own sentence that the public-dataset analysis "validates the relevance of our study in vivo" is an overstatement — that section is purely in-silico re-analysis; the paper contains no in vivo experiment. || [adversarial] The auditor was required (A.4) to hunt the canonical "pre-existing subset selected/expanded rather than converted" alternative and reported it as searched-and-not-found. It exists, it is directly on-target, and it carries the strongest evidence classes in the field. Three items the auditor missed: (1) STRONGEST MISS — Flommersfeld et al., "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection," Immunity 2021, PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403 (full text already archived locally as /home/user/aaa/refs/D2_PMC8528403.txt). Methods: retroviral fluorescent colour-barcoding of HSCs, retrogenic mice, sorting of SINGLE colour-barcoded CD27+Ly49H+ NK cells, multiplexed adoptive transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- / Klra8-/- / NKp46iCre x R26-LSL-iDTA recipients, serial re-transfer into secondary hosts, plus CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic PARABIOSIS. This is OBS_DIRECT + OBS_TRANSFER class, and it instantiates exactly the alternative: (a) ILC1-like NK cells derive from a PRE-EXISTING, prospectively sortable steady-state CD27+CD62L- subset — single cells sorted from that compartment "exclusively generated CD62L- clones"; (b) section heading "ILC1-like NK cells do not serve as precursors of CD62L+ NK cells" — the two are separate lineages that retain distinct phenotypes through the memory phase and upon reinfection; (c) parabiosis: ILC1-like NK cells "remained almost entirely spleen resident, while cNK cells equilibrated between the two parabionts"; (d) the authors re-analysed HUMAN NK scRNA-seq and found the same bifurcation into two lineages by mutually exclusive CD160/XCL1 vs GZMB. So the tissue-resident ILC1-like group-1 ILC phenotype maps onto a pre-existing lineage, not a conversion endpoint. (2) The field's own flagship in vivo conversion paper concedes the definitive assays FAILED. Park et al., "Toxoplasma gondii infection drives conversion of NK cells into ILC1-like cells," eLife 2019, PMID 31393266 / PMC6703900 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC6703900.txt), states verbatim: "an Eomes fate-mapping mouse, that is, EomesCre, could be used to identify a cell-intrinsic role for Eomes, this was not possible due to the ubiquitous expression of Eomes during development (data not shown)" and "Another approach would be to examine Eomes downregulation following adoptive transfer of congenic NK cells prior to infection but this was hindered due to the inability to find transferred cells after 14 d.p.i. (data not shown)." They retreated to Ncr1iCre Eomes-fl/fl mixed BM chimeras. Consequences: NK-to-ILC1 conversion has never been established by OBS_DIRECT anywhere, and their own data show a pre-existing Eomes-INDEPENDENT CD49a+ ILC1 pool that expands on infection ("mild ILC1 expansion occurs in the absence of NK cells") — i.e. part of the ILC1-like pool is selected/expanded, not converted. Also in tension with Picant: "culture of purified NK cells from infected mice did not result in Eomes downregulation," implying cell-extrinsic requirements absent from Picant's purified-NK culture. (3) Sojka et al., eLife 2014, PMID 24714492 — parabiosis plus transcription-factor-deficient mice show liver/uterine/skin CD49a+DX5- tissue-resident NK are cell lineages DISTINCT from conventional splenic and thymic NK. CD49a+ group-1 ILCs have an independent developmental origin, so detecting CD49a+ cells does not license an ex-NK inference. Gao is paywalled (lit.py returns ABSTRACT_ONLY, no PMCID); the abstract describes "global transcriptomic and flow-cytometry analyses and genetically engineered mouse models" and does not mention fate mapping. I could not obtain the Gao Methods, so I cannot verify the fate-mapping characterisation and flag it as unsupported rather than false.

crossfield_g4_findings: The invoked general process is TGF-b-driven acquisition of tissue-residency integrins on a circulating lymphocyte. I searched the TRM, ILC and myeloid literatures. All three bear directly, and two of them supply a methodological verdict on the exact assay Picant used. T CELL / TRM — decisive. Zitti et al., Immunity 2023, PMID 37269830 is the precise methodological analogue and it is damaging to Picant's inference. In vitro stimulation of CIRCULATING human blood CD8+CD45RA-CD62L+ T cells with IL-15 + TGF-b induced CD49a and a cytotoxic TRM transcriptional profile, RUNX2- and RUNX3-dependent. Two lessons. First, TGF-b induction of CD49a/CD103 on circulating human lymphocytes is a generic, cross-lineage program — it is not diagnostic of any lineage, so CD9/CD103/CD49a acquisition cannot by itself mean "ILC1." Second and more important: the T cell field did NOT stop at marker induction. It established the precursor-product relationship by TCR CLONAL REPERTOIRE OVERLAP between PAIRED skin and blood samples from the same donors. That clonal step is exactly what converts marker induction into a lineage claim, and it is exactly what Picant lacks. NK cells carry no rearranged receptor, so the clonal shortcut is unavailable to them — which is precisely why the NK field must use retroviral barcoding or congenic transfer (as Flommersfeld PMID 34437840 did) and why a population-frequency comparison between wells is the weakest available design. Note the sting: RUNX2 sits in Picant's own IL-35-upregulated DEG list, alongside ITGA1, ITGAE, CD9, CXCR3/4 — i.e. what Picant labels an "ILC1-like" program is the RUNX-driven TGF-b residency program shared with CD8 TRM, not an ILC1 lineage program. Corroborating, same field: Girard et al., Mucosal Immunol 2024, PMID 38729611 — MAdCAM-1 + retinoic acid + TGF-b induces blood CD8 T cells to express CD103, CD69, CD101, CCR5, CCR9 and a4b7; the authors frame this explicitly as a "TRM-LIKE phenotype" and "a means to expand these cells in vitro," i.e. a phenotype-induction protocol, never a lineage conversion. Mackay et al., Nat Immunol 2013, doi 10.1038/ni.2744 — CD103 on skin TRM requires local IL-15 + TGF-b AFTER epithelial entry; residency markers are microenvironment-imposed, not cell-autonomous identity. Fonseca et al., Nat Immunol 2020, PMID 32066954 — TRM are not terminally committed: reactivated TRM rejoin the circulating pool and ex-TRM redifferentiate into TCM and TEM. This directly undercuts Picant's headline word "irreversible," which rests on a 48-hour washout during which the cells were still producing autocrine TGF-b; the home field shows this class of differentiation state reverses over weeks, not hours. Fung et al., Sci Immunol 2022, PMID 36332012 — CD103 fate mapping shows CD103 expression is itself dynamic and CD103- TRM are the primary responders; CD103 is a fluctuating state marker, not a stable lineage label. ILC. Gasteiger et al., Science 2015, PMID 26472762 — parabiosis shows ILCs in lymphoid and non-lymphoid organs are tissue-resident, maintained and expanded LOCALLY by self-renewal, with only partial hematogenous replenishment late after infection. Tissue ILC1 pools are largely self-sustaining, so intratumoral ILC1-like cells need not be ex-NK. MYELOID — the cautionary precedent, and the single most instructive one. Ginhoux et al., Science 2010, PMID 20966214 and Hashimoto et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23601688. The "circulating monocytes convert into tissue-resident macrophages" model stood as dogma for decades on precisely this evidence structure: marker similarity plus in vitro differentiation of blood monocytes into macrophage-like cells bearing tissue-macrophage markers. Parabiosis and genetic fate mapping overturned it. Hashimoto's own framing: "Despite accumulating evidence suggesting local self-maintenance of tissue macrophages in the steady state, the dogma remains that tissue macrophages derive from monocytes. Using parabiosis and fate-mapping approaches, we confirmed that monocytes do not show significant contribution to tissue macrophages in the steady state." The resident population turned out to be pre-existing, embryonically derived and locally self-renewing, and the in vitro "monocyte-derived macrophage" was a culture phenotype that did not correspond to the in vivo resident cell. That is the exact structural risk in T6, stated by the field that already made the mistake. METHODOLOGICAL VERDICT these fields deliver on the assays used here: bulk population-frequency shifts + residency-integrin flow markers + a self-derived UCell signature cannot discriminate conversion from selection, nor from a reversible TGF-b state. The assays that CAN discriminate — parabiosis, congenic transfer, genetic fate mapping, clonal repertoire overlap, and in humans transplant chimerism plus intravascular labelling — are all established. Critically, the human NK toolkit demonstrably exists: Buggert/Bjorkstrom et al., "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis," Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907, used intravascular labelling, human LIVER TRANSPLANT donor-versus-recipient chimerism, humanized mice, non-human primates and efferent lymph fluid cannulation to show that infiltrating recipient NK cells acquire tissue-residency traits in vivo (partly Runx3-regulated) and that human NK residency is TRANSIENT with lymphatic recirculation. That paper simultaneously (i) supports that circulating human NK CAN acquire residency traits in vivo, (ii) contradicts "irreversible," and (iii) sets the standard of evidence Picant did not attempt.

species: Human (Homo sapiens) for the anchor study. Counter-evidence and adjacent literature audited additionally in mouse (C57BL/6; Ducimetière PNAS 2021, Torcellan Immunity 2024, Horowitz Sci Transl Med 2026) and rhesus macaque (Wu Front Immunol 2022 barcoding).
what_was_measured: In humans, in freshly dissociated surgical material sampled ONCE at the time of resection (single timepoint; no timecourse, no pre-tumour sample — the organ was never observed before the tumour arose), mtscATAC-seq (joint single-cell ATAC + mitochondrial-DNA heteroplasmy) was run on matched tumour, non-involved lung tissue (NILT, non-adjacent, tumour-free on pathology) and PBMC. Readouts measured were: (a) assignment of cells to mtDNA-variant-defined clones by the Mitotrek framework; (b) cell identity from chromatin-accessibility gene scores at NCR1, GNLY, KLRD1, CD3D, CD8A; (c) per-clone cell-type composition; (d) the fraction of clone-sharing cell pairs for each cell-type pair, within a tissue site and across tissue sites. Measured in 10 patients (5 early-stage NSCLC post-lobectomy with tumour+NILT+blood; 5 ovarian cancer with tumour, 3 with matched blood), 23 samples, 218,715 cells. CRITICAL NEGATIVE: no NK-specific tumour-versus-NILT clone-sharing test was performed; no pre-tumour timepoint, no fate mapping, no photoconversion, no parabiosis, no intravascular labelling, no exogenous barcode exists anywhere in this or any other study for this transition.
n_unit: patients (donors): 5 NSCLC patients with matched tumour + non-involved lung + blood, 5 ovarian cancer patients with tumour (3 with matched blood). 23 samples; 218,715 cells. Cells are NOT the unit of replication. The single NK-informative tumour is n=1 patient (ovarian SU-O-005) and the single NK-informative NSCLC cross-site observation is n=1 patient (SU-L-005). controls: Within the anchor study: (1) Mitotrek benchmarked against published full-length scRNA-seq of single-colony-derived HSPCs with ground-truth clonal identity, 2 independent donors, 91.3% and 85.3% clone-assignment accuracy at a deliberate sensitivity cost (39.9%/55.1% assignment vs ~80% in the original study); (2) randomised cell-grouping null showing same-clone cells share a cell type more than chance; (3) matched PBMC as the circulating comparator and NILT as the tumour-free same-organ comparator; (4) explicit artefact controls for solid-tissue mtDNA lineage tracing — variants detected in >20% of cells within a sample discarded, cells assigned to multiple clones excluded, correlated variants collapsed — introduced because the authors found high-heteroplasmy variants shared across lineages in solid tissue but not PBMC, attributed to ambient mtDNA uptake and/or horizontal mitochondrial transfer; (5) clone-assignment rate shown to be uniform across cell types and tissue sites (15–26% tissue, 20–32% PBMC), so NK are not differentially dropped. No parabiosis / no CD45.1-CD45.2 chimera / no Hobit or Ncr1-CreERT2 fate map / no Kaede photoconversion of uninvolved organ / no adoptive transfer — none of these are possible in human surgical material.
strongest_alternative_explanation: De novo acquisition of residency markers by newly recruited circulating NK — i.e. the intratumoural "trNK" was never in the organ before the tumour. Circulating cNK recruited into a tissue acquire a bona fide residency phenotype in situ: Torcellan et al., Immunity 2024 (PMID 38157853, PMC10783803) showed viral and bacterial skin infection recruits cNK that differentiate into Tcf1-hi CD69-hi trNK transcriptionally resembling human tissue CD56bright TCF1-hi NK, Blimp1-dependent. TGF-beta in the TME is sufficient to drive CD49a+CD103+ trNK differentiation from peripheral NK ex vivo (Horowitz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 42090477), and chronic activation alone drives a tissue-resident-LIKE state via KLF2 loss (Blood 2025, PMID 40857665). Under this alternative, CD49a/CD103/CD69/ITGA1/ITGAE on intratumoural NK is a TME-imposed phenotype, not a residency pedigree, and marker identity to organ trNK carries zero lineage information. TWO FURTHER ALTERNATIVES, both with support: (i) TWO INDEPENDENT ORIGINS with no conversion — Ducimetière et al., PNAS 2021 (PMID 34183415) found in mouse liver metastasis that pre-existing liver trILC1 and recruited cNK are non-redundant and functionally partitioned (trILC1 controls metastatic seeding, cNK restrains outgrowth), i.e. the resident and the tumour-active populations are different cells doing different jobs, not one becoming the other; (ii) IN-SITU DIFFERENTIATION FROM IMMATURE PRECURSORS — tumour-infiltrating immature ILCs in colorectal cancer are biased toward ILC1/trNK differentiation (Nat Commun 2026, s41467-026-71085-9), a third origin that also produces trNK-marked intratumoural cells without any pre-existing mature organ trNK. The canonical "pre-existing subset is selected/expanded rather than converted" alternative is therefore not merely unexcluded — it is the better-supported reading, and the recruitment alternative is better supported still.

Two fields have the tools; both have run the experiment; neither returns the clean answer X1 asserts. MYELOID (the field where this exact structural claim is settled). Loyher PL et al., "Macrophages of distinct origins contribute to tumor development in the lung," J Exp Med 2018;215(10):2536-2553, PMID 30201786, PMC6170177 — OA full text retrieved and read (refs/X1_PMC6170177.txt). Pre-existing resident memory can protect against a later tumour: Malik BT et al., Sci Immunol 2017, PMID 28738020 (skin TRM present before melanoma challenge mediate durable immunity); Enamorado M et al., Nat Commun 2017, PMID 28714465 (resident AND circulating memory both required — the interplay, not residency alone); Molodtsov A et al., Immunity 2021, PMID 34525340 (LN TRM against metastatic melanoma). Against local origin of the functional intratumoural effector pool: Yost KE et al., "Clonal replacement of tumor-specific T cells following PD-1 blockade," Nat Med 2019, PMID 31359002 — in the only lineage with a somatic clonal barcode, the clones that expand in the tumour after checkpoint blockade are largely NOT the pre-existing intratumoural clones but novel clones entering from outside. Structural read-across: the population that does the work inside a tumour is substantially replenished from outside even when a bona fide resident pool exists. Nature 2020 did not surface through lit.py under four different query formulations — recorded as searched-and-not-retrieved, NOT as non-existent (G3). ILC. Ducimetiere 2021 (PMID 34183415): trILC1 and cNK non-redundant in liver metastasis. claim_text: Newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK
species: Homo sapiens (primary source: patient tumour resections, non-involved lung tissue and peripheral blood). Counter-evidence/alternative sources audited are Mus musculus (Sojka 2014 parabiosis; Gasteiger 2015 parabiosis; Gao 2017 tumour models).
what_was_measured: In humans, at a SINGLE cross-sectional timepoint (the moment of therapeutic lobectomy / debulking surgery — no time course, no follow-up sample, no longitudinal tracking), joint single-cell chromatin accessibility + mitochondrial-DNA genotype (mtscATAC-seq) was measured on freshly dissociated, UNCULTURED matched tumour, non-involved lung tissue (NILT) and PBMCs from 5 early-stage NSCLC patients (SU-L-001..005) and on matched tumour + PBMC from 5 ovarian cancer patients (SU-O-001..005). Cells were grouped into "clones" by shared low-frequency somatic mtDNA heteroplasmic variants (mgatk calls at <1% pseudobulk frequency; Mitotrek: variants in >20% of a donor's cells or in <3 cells removed; heteroplasmy matrix binarised at 0.07; variants linked into clonotypes by Pearson rho >0.5 across cells; cells assignable to >1 clone DISCARDED; chrM:307-314 homopolymer region excluded). The readout that bears on this claim is the tissue-site distribution of cells belonging to 14 PBMC-enriched clones (>=10 cells each), of which 2 were NK-dominated and came from ONE donor (SU-L-005). NK identity was assigned only by chromatin gene-accessibility score for GNLY/NCR1/KLRD1/CD3D-negative plus Azimuth PBMC-reference label transfer. NO functional or dysfunction readout of NK cells was performed anywhere in the paper — no cytotoxicity, no degranulation/CD107a, no IFN-gamma/TNF production, no inhibitory-receptor or "exhaustion" protein measurement, no TGF-beta-response assay — and the chromatin state of blood-resident versus tumour-resident members of the SAME NK clone was never compared. Verbatim preprint text (the only place the hinted numbers exist): "Among 14 peripheral blood-enriched clones, 10 were dominated by CD8+ T cells and 2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005). Although the majority of cells from these clones were detected in PBMCs (66.0%), smaller fractions were present in tumor (25.3%) and NILT (8.8%), indicating their ability to infiltrate tissue."
n: NK-specific observation: n = 1 donor (SU-L-005), yielding 2 NK-dominated clones. Whole cohort: n = 5 NSCLC + 5 ovarian = 10 donors. (Cell counts, which are NOT the n: 218,715 cells total; 83,371 lung tumour+NILT, 41,587 lung PBMC, 52,154 ovarian tumour, 41,603 ovarian PBMC.)
n_unit: donors (patients); secondary unit = mtDNA clones (2 NK-dominated, out of 14 blood-enriched, out of ~200+ called clones)
controls: Internal patient-matched design (each donor is its own control: PBMC vs tumour vs NILT from the same person, same processing batch). Comparison clone classes: tumour-enriched and NILT-enriched clones, and the 186 non-enriched clones. Useful negative comparator: B/plasma-cell-dominated clones NEVER spanned blood, showing the assay does not force cross-compartment sharing. Method controls: Mitotrek benchmarked against published HSPC colony data with independently known clonal truth (91.3% and 85.3% assignment accuracy in 2 donors); for SU-O-002, orthogonal paired scRNA/TCR-seq on 6,982 cells showed TCR-mtDNA clonotype correspondence; variants >1% pseudobulk frequency excluded as zygotic/developmental; ArchR QC (TSS enrichment >4, >1000 unique fragments) and doublet scoring; multi-clone cells discarded; annotations cross-checked by Azimuth. The authors themselves flag two uncontrolled confounders specific to solid-tumour samples: ambient mtDNA uptake during single-cell capture and horizontal mitochondrial transfer, both of which "are unlikely to reflect bona fide clonal relationships." MISSING CONTROLS relevant to this claim: no non-cancer/healthy donor; no second timepoint; no per-compartment NK-capture-depth normalisation; no orthogonal directional tracer of any kind (no labelling, no transfer, no parabiosis, no intravascular staining); and no dysfunction assay against which a "dysfunctional" endpoint could be defined.
strongest_alternative_explanation: THREE alternatives, each of which fully explains the data without any A->B transition. (1) PARALLEL SEEDING FROM A SHARED PROGENITOR (the canonical "pre-existing subset" alternative, and the strongest here). A shared somatic mtDNA variant proves shared ANCESTRY, not shared TRAJECTORY. strongest_alternative_explanation: Three alternatives, in increasing order of damage. (1) THE END STATE IS NOT A STATE — the primary alternative. Gill et al. state verbatim: "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology." The destination B is constituted by an analogy, not by an observation. If "exhausted NK" just means "an NK cell whose IFN-gamma/cytotoxicity is lower than an arbitrary comparator (usually autologous blood NK)", then "NK -> exhausted NK" is not a lineage transition at all; it is a restatement of a functional measurement with an arrow drawn through it, and no fate question is being answered. Bi & Tian's own pro-exhaustion review concedes "the transcriptional factors specific for exhausted NK cells are yet to be defined"; Judge/Murphy/Canter state "there is no established NK phenotype for these dysfunctional states" and "there remains controversy as to whether NK cells even undergo exhaustion (as opposed to other dysfunction processes), and if so, the phenotypic markers that define an exhausted NK cell." (2) SELECTION, NOT CONVERSION (the canonical alternative, and it fully survives this design). Donor NK cells were transferred as a bulk polyclonal pool into IRRADIATED, lymphopenic hosts and underwent homeostatic proliferation; the paper itself reports that loss of cytotoxicity "progresses with homeostatic proliferation and tumor exposure." Without clonal or barcode tracking, preferential survival and outgrowth of the already-hypofunctional, terminally mature fraction of the input pool (CD27-CD11b+, KLRG1-high) reproduces every observed population-level fall — mean NKG2D, mean Eomes, mean IFN-gamma, mean lysis — with zero individual cells converting. Congenic CD45.1 marking proves the cells are donor-derived; it does not prove they are the same cells that were functional on day 1. Proliferation-coupled decline is exactly what a selection model predicts, so the paper's own kinetic argument cuts against it. (3) TECHNICAL ARTEFACT in the human literature that built the end state after 2012: the flagship marker PD-1 is either not expressed by NK cells at all (Judge 2020) or is physically stolen from tumour cells (Hasim 2022), and enzymatic tumour dissociation with collagenase/dispase is known to cleave lymphocyte surface molecules, so "intratumoural NK have lost their receptors" can be a digestion artefact.

crossfield_g4_findings: I searched the CD8 T cell field (the home field of "exhaustion") and the ILC field. The T cell field established exhaustion as a genuine lineage state via THREE methodological anchors. NK "exhaustion" has none of them, and on the one anchor that has been directly tested in NK cells the answer came back NEGATIVE. ANCHOR 1 — EPIGENETIC FIXITY IS THE CRITERION THAT SEPARATES EXHAUSTION FROM REVERSIBLE TUNING. Sen DR et al., "The epigenetic landscape of T cell exhaustion," Science 2016, PMID 27789799, defined exhaustion-specific enhancers distinct from effector and memory states; Pauken KE et al., "Epigenetic stability of exhausted T cells limits durability of reinvigoration by PD-1 blockade," Science 2016, PMID 27789795, showed the chromatin state is NOT remodelled by checkpoint blockade, which is why reinvigoration is transient. This is precisely what makes "T cell becomes exhausted T cell" a lineage claim rather than a description of low function. Gill 2012 performed NO chromatin or DNA-methylation assay. Worse, the direct NK test of fixity exists and is negative: Elliott 2010 (PMID 20819924) shows mature NK hyporesponsiveness reverses completely in ~4 days in vivo without division. Under the T cell field's own criterion, that is tuning/anergy, not exhaustion. ANCHOR 2 — THE PRECURSOR-PRODUCT HIERARCHY WAS ESTABLISHED BY SORTED-SUBSET ADOPTIVE TRANSFER, NOT BULK TRANSFER. Im SJ et al., Nature 2016, PMID 27501248; Utzschneider DT et al., Immunity 2016, PMID 27533016; Miller BC et al., Nat Immunol 2019, PMID 30778252; Beltra JC et al., "Developmental Relationships of Four Exhausted CD8+ T Cell Subsets...", Immunity 2020, PMID 32396847. In every case a candidate PROGENITOR (TCF1+/PD-1+) was sorted, transferred, and shown to give rise to the candidate TERMINAL product. That is the experiment that licenses an arrow. Gill transferred BULK polyclonal NK and re-read the same pool — it never sorted a candidate precursor state and showed it yields a candidate product state. This is the decisive G4 finding: the missing experiment is not exotic, it is the same adoptive-transfer technique Gill already had in hand, and no one has run it for NK "exhaustion". Note this also means my DOWNGRADE is not merely semantic — the T cell field draws exactly this line between bulk-population kinetics and a demonstrated lineage step. ANCHOR 3 — A TF THAT ENFORCES THE STATE AND IS DISPENSABLE FOR DEVELOPMENT. Khan O et al., "TOX transcriptionally and epigenetically programs CD8+ T cell exhaustion," Nature 2019, PMID 31207603 (with Scott/Alfei companions). In NK cells TOX is a lineage-specification requirement — Aliahmad P et al., Nat Immunol 2010, PMID 20818394 — so the borrowed concept's defining enforcer has an incompatible job in the borrowing lineage. This confirms the auditor's point; the auditor had this one right. CONSENSUS: Blank CU et al., "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'," Nat Rev Immunol 2019;19:665-674, PMID 31570879 — confirmed real and located. Its four anchors (chronic antigen stimulation through a clonotypic receptor; hierarchical progressive functional loss; TCF1+ progenitor to TCF1- terminal hierarchy; TOX-driven epigenetic enforcement separating exhaustion from anergy and senescence) are satisfied by NK exhaustion with direct evidence in ZERO cases.
